pacific-tonga-tui.source: Historical Basemaps Tu'i Tonga Empire 1200-1500 (PARTOF=Tu'i Tonga Empire); Wikipedia 'Tu'i Tonga Empire'
pacific-tonga-tui.rationale: Current polygons cover only Tongatapu, Ha'apai and Vava'u — the Tu'i Tonga thalassocracy's claimed tributary zone (Samoa, Niue, Wallis & Futuna, eastern Fiji/Lau) is missing. Added simplified polygons per HBM extent.

pacific-samoan.source: Wikipedia 'Samoan Islands'; Brij Lal & Kate Fortune, Pacific Islands: An Encyclopedia (2000)
pacific-samoan.rationale: Current geometry covers only Western Samoa (Savai'i + Upolu). Samoan polity / cultural extent must include Tutuila and Manu'a — these were the homeland of Tui Manu'a and the Manu'an branch.

pacific-maori.rationale: Existing 14-polygon MultiPolygon already covers North Island, South Island, Stewart Island, Chatham Islands, and NZ sub-Antarctic islands — bbox (-176.9, -52.6) to (178.8, -34.4) is correct for Maori cultural domain (Aotearoa + Rekohu + sub-Antarctic). No change required.

pacific-tahitian.source: Wikipedia 'Kingdom of Tahiti' and 'Pomare dynasty'; Britannica 'Pomare II'
pacific-tahitian.rationale: Current geometry includes Marquesas Islands (north of lat -12) which were NEVER under Pomare authority — Marquesas were independent valley-chiefdoms until French annexation 1842. Removed Marquesas polygons; added Tuamotu and Austral representative atolls.

pacific-hawaiian-kingdom.source: Wikipedia 'Hawaiian Kingdom'; NPS 'Archeology of the Mystery Islands Nihoa and Mokumanamana' (1857 annexation by Kamehameha IV)
pacific-hawaiian-kingdom.rationale: Current geometry only covered 8 main Hawaiian Islands. The Kingdom's formal extent under Kamehameha IV (1857) included the entire Hawaiian archipelago from Hawai'i Island in the southeast to Kure Atoll in the northwest. Added Nihoa, Mokumanamana (Necker), French Frigate Shoals, Gardner Pinnacles, Laysan, Lisianski, Pearl & Hermes, and Kure. Midway excluded (taken by USA 1867, never Hawaiian).

asia-xiongnu.rationale: Current hand-crafted polygon (Mongolian Plateau + western Manchuria to Liao River + Hexi/Ordos + outer Tarim oases as tributaries, bbox 80,37.2,124,53) matches Wikipedia/Britannica description of Xiongnu under Modu Chanyu (eastern Liao River, western Pamirs/Tarim, north to Baikal, south to Great Wall). Does not over-include Xinjiang—Tarim oases were tributary, not core territory. HBM 'Xiongnu' bbox is biased eastward (85-131) which over-extends into Manchuria and under-extends west; current hand-crafted is preferable.

asia-xianbei.rationale: Xianbei under Tanshihuai (c.156-181 CE) inherited and slightly expanded the Xiongnu range with deeper Manchurian penetration. Current bbox 85,39.5,129,52.5 matches scholarly maps (Cambridge History of China vol 1). HBM only provides 'Southern Xiongnu' for years 100/200, a different polity confined to Ordos/Hexi—not a substitute. Keep hand-crafted geometry.
sources: Cambridge History of China vol. 1, ch. 6

asia-rouran.rationale: Rouran Khaganate at peak under Shelun (c.402) and his successors held Mongolian Plateau north of the Northern Wei border, Jungaria/Altai west, Greater Khingan east. Current bbox 82,41,124,52.5 matches Cambridge Inner Asia atlas. No canonical HBM feature available (HBM jumps from Xiongnu to Gokturk era). Hand-crafted is the best-available source.
sources: Sinor (ed.) Cambridge History of Early Inner Asia, ch. 11

asia-first-turkic-gokturk.rationale: First Turkic Khaganate under Muqan Khan (553-572) at peak stretched from Manchuria/Greater Khingan to the lower Volga and Crimean steppe. Current bbox 48,39,125,55 captures this Caspian-to-Manchuria span as required (Black Sea reach is via vassal alliance with Byzantium not direct territory, so western 48° is defensible). HBM does not provide First Turkic Khaganate; only the 700 successor 'Western Gokturk Khaganate' which is a tiny remnant fragment. Hand-crafted geometry is canonical.
sources: Golden, Introduction to the History of the Turkic Peoples (1992) maps

asia-eastern-gokturk.rationale: Eastern Göktürk Khaganate (603-630, restored 682-744). Current bbox 85,40.2,124,53 matches the post-split eastern realm: Mongolian Plateau core, Greater Khingan east, Altai west, Tang frontier south. HBM has no specific feature; hand-crafted polygon is best-available.
sources: Cambridge History of China vol. 3, ch. 5

asia-western-gokturk.rationale: Western Göktürk Khaganate (603-657) under Tong Yabghu reached from the Aral/lower Volga to the Hindu Kush, controlling Sogdiana and the Silk Road oases. Current bbox 40,38,85,54 captures Pontic-Caspian steppe to Tarim. HBM 'Western Gokturk Khaganate' at year 700 (bbox 59-60, 44-46) is a post-collapse remnant fragment, not the empire's peak; hand-crafted is preferable.
sources: Golden, Introduction to the History of the Turkic Peoples (1992)

asia-eastern-gokturk-second.rationale: Second Eastern Türk Khaganate (682-744) under Bilge Khan and Tonyukuk restored the eastern Türk realm to roughly its first-period extent. Current bbox 85,40.2,124,53 is essentially identical to the first-period eastern khanate—appropriate given continuity. HBM offers no specific feature.
sources: Orkhon inscriptions; Sinor, Cambridge History of Early Inner Asia

asia-uyghur-khaganate.rationale: Uyghur Khaganate (744-840) succeeded the Türks on the Mongolian Plateau, capital at Ordu-Baliq (Karabalghasun) on the Orkhon. Current bbox 85,40.3,123,52.5 matches the Orkhon-based khaganate. HBM 'Uyghurs' (700, bbox 76-99, 36.5-40.6) describes the Tarim Uyghurs post-840 collapse, not the Khaganate—NOT a substitute. Keep hand-crafted.
sources: Mackerras, The Uighur Empire According to the T'ang Dynastic Histories

asia-khazar.rationale: Current geometry is 'reconstructed-clipped-country' with 664 vertices—built from modern country outlines, not historical cartography. Replaced with historical-basemaps 'Khazars' (year 800) feature which captures the canonical 8th-century peak: lower Volga (Atil/Itil capital) to Dnieper, Crimea/Caucasus to mid-Don, with Aral-Caspian steppe tributaries. Matches Wikipedia/Britannica description.

asia-pechenegs.rationale: Pechenegs (860-1091) occupied the Pontic-Caspian steppe between Volga and Danube. Current bbox 24,44,54,52 spans this canonical range. HBM 'Pechenegs' at year 900 (bbox 31.5-36.3, 48.6-50.7) shows only the Ukrainian core, omitting the broader steppe range described in Constantine Porphyrogenitus 'De Administrando Imperio' (8 Pecheneg themes from Don to Danube). Hand-crafted is more accurate to scholarship.
sources: Constantine VII Porphyrogenitus, De Administrando Imperio (10th c.)

asia-cumans-kipchaks.rationale: Current geometry (561 verts, 'reconstructed-clipped-country') is built from clipped modern country shapes. Replaced with HBM 'Cuman Khanates' (1200) which is the canonical Cuman-Kipchak confederation polygon for its pre-Mongol peak: Danube/Carpathians west, Aral-Irtysh east, mid-Volga north, Caucasus south. Bbox 28.6-65.9, 39.7-57.2 matches Golden's mapping in Cambridge History of Inner Asia.
sources: Golden, 'The Cuman-Qipchaqs' in Cambridge History of Inner Asia

asia-khwarezmian.rationale: Current bbox covers Iran (44 E westward Caspian region) through Transoxiana to ~80 E. / Period 1077-1231 spans both the early vassal Khwarazmshahs and the full empire under Muhammad II (1200-1220). / At peak (1218): Iran + Khorasan + Transoxiana + Afghanistan + into Punjab (Indus, ~70 E). Current bbox max east at 80 E is too far east (Khwarezmians never reached central India).
asia-khwarezmian.hbm_reference: No specific Khwarezmian layer in HBM. Source field says 'reconstructed-clipped-country' — looks OK but eastern bound 80 E is over-extended past the Indus.

asia-kara-khitai.rationale: Current bbox (63.8-92.8, 34.6-50.9) is reasonable but uses 'reconstructed-clipped-country' methodology. HBM 'Kara Khitai Khaganate' (1200, bbox 53.2-88.8, 33.1-56.5) is the canonical historical-basemaps feature for the empire's pre-Khwarezm/Naiman-flank period, with a more accurate Semirechye-and-eastern-Khwarezm western limit and Altai/Lake Balkhash northern reach. Replace with HBM.
sources: Biran, The Empire of the Qara Khitai in Eurasian History (2005)

mongol-empire.rationale: CRITICAL FIX: current geometry has 8191 vertices and bbox [-180,18.17,180,81.86]—it spans BOTH HEMISPHERES, clearly a broken global polygon (probably an inverted antimeridian artifact). Replaced with union of the four 1279 HBM khanate features (Great Khanate/Yuan + Chagatai + Ilkhanate + Golden Horde). The resulting bbox (22.5°E Hungary border to 141°E Sea of Japan, 19.7°N S China/Hainan to 62.5°N Arctic) matches the canonical Mongol Empire peak (~1279, post-Song conquest, pre-Yuan disintegration) and the description as the largest contiguous land empire ever.
sources: historical-basemaps world_1279.geojson (Great Khanate + Chagatai Khanate + Ilkhanate + Khanate of the Golden Horde, unioned)

asia-chagatai-khanate.rationale: Current geometry (bbox 46.5-91.7, 35.1-55.4) over-extends westward into modern Iraq/Caucasus, which were Ilkhanate not Chagatai. HBM 'Chagatai Khanate' (1300, bbox 60.0-93.8, 31.8-50.4) accurately captures the central-Asian khanate (Transoxiana, Semirechye, Tarim, parts of Afghanistan) without trespassing on Ilkhanate territory. Replace with HBM.
sources: Biran in Cambridge History of Inner Asia (Chinggisid Age)

asia-golden-horde.rationale: Current 'reconstructed-clipped-country' (bbox 23.4-87.3, 40.6-57.9) is built from modern country outlines. HBM 'Khanate of the Golden Horde' (1300, bbox 22.5-94.0, 38.9-62.5) is the canonical historical-basemaps feature: Carpathians/Danube west, Aral-Irtysh-Ob east, mid-Volga and Siberian forest line north, Caucasus/Khwarezm south. Captures the broader Jochid ulus including Blue Horde holdings in West Siberia.
sources: historical-basemaps world_1300.geojson 'Khanate of the Golden Horde'
Halperin, Russia and the Golden Horde (1985)

asia-ilkhanate.rationale: Current bbox (26.1-72.1, 25.1-43.6) over-extends west into central Anatolia (26°E) which was Seljuk-Rûm/Byzantine, not Ilkhanate (which held eastern Anatolia and the Rûm Sultanate as vassal). HBM 'Ilkhanate' (1300, bbox 35.8-69.8, 23.9-42.6) gives the canonical extent: Iran + Iraq + Caucasus + eastern Anatolia + western Afghanistan. Matches Hülegüid borders described in Cambridge History of Iran vol. 5.
sources: Cambridge History of Iran, vol. 5 (Saljuq and Mongol periods)

timurid-empire.rationale: Current bbox (53.9-72.0, 26.5-46.3) is far too narrow—covers only Iran/Transoxiana, OMITS Timur's conquests in Mesopotamia (Baghdad 1401), Anatolia (Ankara 1402), Caucasus, and North India (Delhi 1398). HBM 'Timurid Empire' (1400, bbox 35.8-76.2, 23.9-46.4) correctly extends from Euphrates to Indus, Caucasus to Persian Gulf, matching Britannica/Wikipedia descriptions of Timur's empire on his death in 1405. Replace.
sources: Manz, The Rise and Rule of Tamerlane (1989)

tibetan-empire.rationale: Current geometry (bbox 77.2-102.4, 26.3-37.1) matches modern Tibet Autonomous Region outlines—it OMITS the 8th-9th-century imperial conquests: Tarim Basin (the Tibetans held Khotan, Kashgar, Kucha from 670s-790s), the Gansu Corridor (briefly took Chang'an in 763), and large parts of modern Sichuan and Yunnan. HBM 'Tibetan Empire' (800, bbox 75.2-104.3, 21.9-43.8) correctly includes Tarim northward extension to 43.8°N and Gansu/Sichuan eastward to 104.3°E. Matches Beckwith, 'The Tibetan Empire in Central Asia' (1987). Replace.
sources: Beckwith, The Tibetan Empire in Central Asia (1987)

asia-dzungar-khanate.rationale: Current bbox covers Dzungaria (modern N. Xinjiang, ~80-95 E, ~42-50 N) plus surroundings. / At peak (Galdan ~1680s): also held Tarim basin (E. Turkestan, ~74-90 E, 36-42 N), parts of Mongolia, Kazakh steppe encroachments. / Bbox 73.35-101.23 E, 35-50.58 N is reasonable as upper envelope. / Note: Dzungars are Mongol/Buddhist, not Islamic — inclusion in 'islamic_middle_east' subset is questionable. May be a Central Asian cross-listing. / Generally accurate. Could exclude Tibet (where bbox 35 N south reaches close to Tibetan plateau).

rashidun-caliphate.rationale: Hand-traced peak Rashidun (~656 CE): Arabia + Levant + Egypt + Cyrenaica + Mesopotamia + Iran/Khorasan. Earlier pass had wrongly assigned Umayyad-700 (too large; includes al-Andalus + Maghreb + Sindh).

umayyad-caliphate.rationale: Pulled from HBM in pass 2 (matched Umayyad Caliphate in 700).

umayyad-cordoba.rationale: Pulled from HBM in pass 2 (matched Caliphate of Córdoba in 1000).

abbasid-caliphate.rationale: Current bbox is excellent — covers Maghreb (Ifriqiya, Aghlabid vassal) to Transoxiana/Sindh. / Minor: Abbasids lost al-Andalus to Umayyad survivors (Cordoba) in 756 — should NOT cover Iberia, and current bbox does exclude it. Good. / Minor: by 800 CE, Idrisids (788) controlled western Maghreb; effective Abbasid control did not reach west of Ifriqiya (Tunisia, ~10 E). Current bbox starts at 19 E which is conservative — fine. / Vertex count of 605 indicates good detail.

fatimid-caliphate.rationale: Current bbox tracks HBM 1000/1100/1200 (identical bbox) — covers Egypt, Maghreb (early), Hejaz, parts of Levant. / Possible over-extent: by 1100 the Fatimids had effectively lost the Maghreb to the Zirids/Hammadids (broke with Cairo 1048) and Sicily to the Normans (by 1091). The polygon for late Fatimid period (post-1100) should NOT include central/western Maghreb. HBM repeats the 1000 extent for all three centuries which is itself questionable, but matches the existing geometry. / Sicily (~13-15 E) is correctly NOT in bbox if HBM 1000 starts at 0.5 E (suggests Maghreb but Sicily had Fatimid suzerainty until ~970).

mena-ayyubid-sultanate.rationale: Pulled from HBM in pass 2 (matched Ayyubid Sultanate in 1200).

mena-mamluk-sultanate.rationale: Current bbox matches HBM world_1279/1300 'Mamluke Sultanate' exactly. Egypt + Levant + Hejaz + part of Cyrenaica. / Northern bound at 36.3 N is correct — Mamluks did not control Anatolia (border with Karamanids / Ottomans was south of Taurus). / Yemen NOT included — correct: Mamluks did not directly rule Yemen for most of the period (Rasulids 1229-1454, then Tahirids). / Maghreb NOT included — correct (Hafsids in Tunisia, etc.). / Minor: Mamluk southern frontier with Nubia was around 22 N (Aswan) but Christian Nubia persisted to 1500s — current 19.68 N is too far south, encroaching on Makuria/Alodia/Funj. Should clip to ~22 N south of Egypt.

mena-great-seljuk.rationale: Pulled from HBM in pass 2 (matched Seljuk Empire in 1100).

mena-seljuk-rum.rationale: Current bbox covers central+eastern Anatolia. Reasonable approximation of the post-Manzikert / pre-Köse Dağ Sultanate (~1200 peak). / Eastern bound at 41.5 E reaches around Erzincan but should reach Lake Van region (~43.4 E) at peak (~1230 under Ala' al-Din Kayqubad I). / Western bound at 29 E excludes the Aegean coast which was lost to Byzantines/Crusaders after 1097 — appropriate for the post-1100 Sultanate (which had retreated from the Aegean). / Southern bound at 36 N reasonable (Mediterranean / Cilician Armenian frontier).
mena-seljuk-rum.hbm_reference: world_1300.geojson 'Seljuk Caliphate' — note HBM mis-labels this as 'Caliphate' but geometry is the Sultanate of Rum (bbox 29-41.5 E, 36-42 N).

asia-ghaznavid-empire.rationale: Pulled from HBM in pass 2 (matched Ghaznavid Emirate in 1100).

asia-ghurid-empire.rationale: The startYear of 879 is anachronistic — Ghurids were a minor Afghan polity until the mid-12th c.; their imperial expansion was 1149-1215. Date range needs review (probably should be 1148-1215, not 879). / Current polygon (58 vtx) is a tiny disc centered on Ghor / central Afghanistan (~64-70 E, 29-37.5 N) — only the homeland. / At peak (~1202-1206 under Ghiyath al-Din and Mu'izz al-Din): empire spanned Khorasan (Nishapur ~58 E) in the west to Bengal (~88 E) in the east, and from Gorgan/Caspian (~37 N) south to Multan/Sindh (~28 N). / Punjab (Lahore conquered 1186), Delhi (1192), Ajmer, Gwalior, Bengal (1202-3) all missing. / Western Iran additions: Bestam, Qumes (~54-55 E) missing.
asia-ghurid-empire.hbm_reference: None — HBM has no Ghurid layer. Build from Wikipedia/Britannica.

almoravid-empire.rationale: Current bbox matches HBM world_1100 'Almoravid dynasty' exactly. / Covers western Sahel (Senegal river region ~17 W), Maghreb (Morocco, western Algeria), and southern al-Andalus to ~42 N. / Reasonable approximation of c. 1110 peak. Excludes far-eastern Almoravid raids that didn't establish lasting rule.

almohad-caliphate.rationale: Pulled from HBM in pass 2 (matched Almohad Caliphate in 1200).

ottoman-early.rationale: Hand-traced end-of-period Ottoman (1453): Balkans south of Danube + NW Anatolia + Aegean coast. Earlier pass had assigned 1500 polygon (too large; includes Egypt/Levant/Mesopotamia that came under Selim I in 1517).

ottoman-mid.rationale: Current bbox covers from Algeria (Algiers, ~3 E was Ottoman from 1529 — bbox extends to -1.5 E covering Oran/W Algeria) east to Mesopotamia/Caucasus (48.5 E) and north to Hungary (48.5 N) south to Yemen (12.6 N). / This bbox is essentially the full Suleimanic Ottoman extent (which extends 1566) — entirely appropriate for the *end* of this period; OK to label as 'mid' covering 1453-1566. / Minor: 1453 saw a much smaller empire (no Egypt yet — Selim I 1517; no Mesopotamia — 1534; no Hungary — 1526). The single bbox necessarily represents end-period peak.

ottoman-peak.rationale: Identical bbox/geometry to ottoman-mid (vtx 1345 both). Reflects the Suleiman-to-pre-Vienna peak. / Notable additions to mid: Cyprus (1571), Yemen (re-secured 1568, lost late), Crete (1669, near end of period), Podolia (1672). Current bbox already includes these via extent. / Could include Crimea as vassal (current bbox doesn't reach 50 N which is correct — Crimea reached only ~49 N peninsula proper; bbox at 48.6 N covers main Crimea).

ottoman-late.rationale: Current bbox tracks post-1699 (Karlowitz) extent — Hungary lost (so western bound 15.75 E starts in Balkans, reasonable). / Eastern bound 50.97 E covers far-east Mesopotamia/Mosul region (held until 1918). / Southern bound 19.68 N covers Hejaz/Yemen (held until WWI). / Northern 48.94 N covers Bosnia/Hercegovina/Belgrade (lost 1878-1908). / Period spans 240 years of progressive territorial loss; the single bbox represents an upper envelope, OK as static layer. / Maghreb component (Algiers/Tunis/Tripoli) included to 15.75 E. Egypt's khedivate (de jure Ottoman) included.

safavid-empire.rationale: Pulled from HBM in pass 2 (matched Safavid Empire in 1600).

asia-afsharid-dynasty.rationale: Current polygon is a tiny oval centered on central Iran (51-57 E, 26.5-37.7 N) — basically just Isfahan-Yazd corridor + Caspian strip. / Nadir Shah's empire at peak (1739-1747) was VAST: encompassed Iran proper + Iraq + Caucasus (Georgia, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Dagestan) + all Afghanistan + parts of Pakistan (Sindh, Punjab to Delhi briefly 1739) + Turkmenistan + Uzbekistan (Bukhara and Khiva subjugated 1740) + parts of Oman/Bahrain. / Bbox should be approximately [42, 24, 78, 42] to cover from Iraq west to Indus east and Caucasus north. / After 1747 (Nadir's assassination), empire collapsed rapidly; effective Afsharid control by 1750 was reduced to Khorasan only. So the 1736-1796 span includes both a vast peak and a tiny rump.
asia-afsharid-dynasty.hbm_reference: No direct Afsharid layer in HBM (transition between world_1715 and world_1783 misses 1747 peak). Build from Wikipedia Afsharid map.

asia-zand-dynasty.rationale: Current bbox 51-57 E, 26.5-36 N is the same generic central-Iran oval as Afsharid/Qajar — clearly a placeholder. / At peak (1751-1779 under Karim Khan), the Zands controlled most of Iran except Khorasan (which remained under Afsharid then independent), plus parts of Iraq (held Basra 1776-1779) and nominal suzerainty over Caucasian khanates (Georgia, Armenia, Azerbaijan). / Bbox should be approximately [44, 25, 60, 41] — westward to include Iraq (Basra ~47.8 E) and parts of Caucasus (north to ~41 N), eastward to Khorasan frontier (~60 E).
asia-zand-dynasty.hbm_reference: No direct Zand layer in HBM. Approximate from Wikipedia Zand dynasty map.

asia-qajar-dynasty.rationale: Pulled from HBM in pass 2 (matched Persia in 1800).

crimean-khanate.rationale: Pulled from HBM in pass 2 (matched Crimean Khanate in 1500).

asia-khanate-bukhara.rationale: Current bbox covers core Transoxiana from Khorasan frontier (58.6 E) to Tashkent area (72.7 E), Balkh-Termez south (35.1 N) to Aral/Syr Darya region (41.97 N). / Reasonable for the Shaybanid/Janid Khanate of Bukhara at most periods (1500-1740). / HBM world_1530 'Bukara Khanate' bbox [68.8, 35.6, 84.5, 42.5] is shifted significantly east and north — that HBM extent reaches into Kyrgyzstan/Xinjiang which is wrong (Tashkent at 69.3 E should be eastern edge). / Current geometry seems more historically accurate than HBM's. Keep current.
asia-khanate-bukhara.hbm_reference: HBM world_1530 'Bukara Khanate' (bbox 68.8-84.5 E) is actually mis-extended east — current geometry is preferable.

asia-khanate-khiva.rationale: Current bbox 56-64.5 E, 37-44 N covers the lower Amu Darya / Khwarazm oasis and adjoining Karakum. / Khiva's historical territory included most of modern Turkmenistan (controlled by various periods) — western frontier extended toward the Caspian (~53-54 E at peak); current bbox at 55.98 E cuts off the Caspian/Mangyshlak coast which Khiva claimed. / Southern bound 36.93 N excludes the Turkmen tribal areas south to ~36 N (Tejen valley, Ashkhabad region) which were nominally Khivan. / Northern bound 43.95 N reasonable (Aral sea ~45 N north shore). / Note: HBM world_1600 'Khiva Khanate' has a bizarre bbox [50.3, 36.3, 107.3, 76.4] — clearly a topology error (lat reaching 76 N is impossible). HBM data is unreliable for this polity.
asia-khanate-khiva.hbm_reference: HBM world_1600.geojson 'Khiva Khanate' has invalid bbox extending to 76 N — DO NOT USE.

asia-khanate-kokand.rationale: Current bbox 68.6-78.2 E, 37.8-43 N covers the Fergana valley + surrounding mountains. / At peak (~1830-1840 under Madali Khan), Kokand extended much further: /   - Northwest to Aq Masjed/Kyzylorda (~65.5 E) — the western frontier /   - North to the Ulu Tau Mountains (~67 E, 48 N) — the northern frontier (central Kazakhstan) /   - South to Sariqol/Tāšqurḡān (~75 E, 39 N) in modern Xinjiang /   - East to Karakol on Issyk Kul (~78 E) / Current bbox correctly captures eastern bound (78 E) but truncates west (should be 65 E, not 68.6 E) and north (should be 48 N, not 43 N). / Tashkent (69.3 E, 41 N) was conquered 1800 — included.
asia-khanate-kokand.hbm_reference: No direct Kokand layer in HBM. The 'central Asian khanates' aggregate is too broad.

durrani-empire.rationale: Current polygon (21 vtx) is a thin horizontal sliver from 60 E to 75.5 E, lat 36.3-38.5 N — covers only a narrow band across northern Afghanistan (Hindu Kush foothills). / This is totally wrong. The Durrani Empire at peak (1761 under Ahmad Shah after Third Battle of Panipat) covered: /   - Modern Afghanistan (full: ~60-75 E, ~29-39 N) /   - Northeastern Iran (Khorasan, Mashhad area ~57-60 E) /   - Most of Pakistan (Sindh, Baluchistan, Punjab — ~64-76 E, ~24-34 N) /   - Kashmir (~74-78 E, ~33-35 N) /   - Briefly to Delhi (~77 E, 28.6 N) after Panipat 1761 /   - Eastern Turkmenistan (Panjdeh oasis ~63 E, 36 N) / Bbox should be approximately [57, 24, 78, 39]. Current bbox misses Sindh/Baluchistan/Kashmir entirely.
durrani-empire.hbm_reference: No specific Durrani layer in HBM (period 1747-1826 is between world_1715 and world_1783). Approximate from world_1783 'central Asian khanates' is too broad/inadequate. Build from Wikipedia.

mughal-early.rationale: Current bbox (64.2-83.8E, 24.0-38.2N) matches HBM 'Mughal Empire'@1530 (Babur era) exactly — north Indo-Gangetic plain from Kabul to Bihar.

asia-mughal-akbar.rationale: Current geometry extends south to 8N (Cape Comorin/Madurai), which Akbar never reached. Per Schwartzberg and audit guidance, Akbar's southern boundary was the Krishna river area; northern reach Kandahar/Kabul. HBM Mughal Empire@1600 (64.2-83.8E, 24.0-38.2N) represents Akbar's canonical extent at his peak.

mughal-peak.rationale: Current bbox (65.5-92.6E, 11.4-38.0N) matches HBM 'Mughal Empire'@1700 (Aurangzeb peak) exactly. Southern reach ~11.4N (deep Deccan after 1687 conquests) — appropriate for the empire's greatest extent.

asia-mughal-aurangzeb.rationale: Current geometry extends south to 6.74N (Travancore/Sri Lanka), which Aurangzeb never reached. Per audit critical guidance: 'Aurangzeb (~1700) reached Deccan but never the deep south (Travancore/Madurai).' HBM Mughal@1700 stops at 11.35N (Tanjore frontier) — the accurate southern limit.

mughal-late.rationale: Current bbox (65.5-92.6E, 11.4-38.0N) matches HBM Mughal@1715 — nominal extent in the immediate post-Aurangzeb era before mid-18th c decline. Border style downgraded to dashed since post-1707 the empire was largely nominal — most territory was Maratha/Nizam de facto.

asia-sikh-empire.rationale: Current bbox (67.7-79.0E, 27.4-36.8N) — Punjab, Kashmir, Khyber Pass, parts of Sindh, NW Tibet — matches HBM 'Sikhs'@1800 closely. Appropriate for Ranjit Singh's peak.

eastern-roman-byzantine-early.rationale: Eastern Roman 395-600. HBM 500 Eastern Roman Empire captures the post-Theodosian division before Justinian's reconquests; current polygon is identical to this. Verified-unchanged.

europe-frankish-kingdom.rationale: Frankish realm 481-843. Current polygon is a 5-vertex placeholder around Cologne; replaced with Ourednik's Carolingian Empire at 800 CE (the canonical peak under Charlemagne).

byzantine-justinian.rationale: Justinian I peak 527-565. Use HBM 600 Eastern Roman Empire (records Justinian's reconquests of Italy, S Spain, N Africa as still present) — current polygon misses Italy/Africa/Spain.

europe-bulgarian-first.rationale: CRITICAL: current geometry is located on the Volga River (bbox 47-58 lon, 51-58 lat) — that is the Volga Bulgars, an unrelated polity. First Bulgarian Empire 681-1018 was in the BALKANS. Replaced with Ourednik 800 Bulgars (Balkan Danubian Bulgaria).

europe-venetian-republic.rationale: Venice 697-1797. Use Ourednik 1500 Venice — Stato da Tera (NE Italy) + Stato da Mar (Istria, Dalmatia, Ionian Is., Crete). Cyprus added 1489 — included in HBM 1500 Venice bbox.

papal-states.rationale: Papal States 756-1870. Use Ourednik 1530 — Lazio, Umbria, Marche, Romagna; post-Borgia consolidation.

carolingian-empire.rationale: Carolingian Empire at 800 CE. Existing polygon is already well-sourced (vtx=371); refreshed against Ourednik 800 CE for consistency with Frankish predecessor.

kingdom-of-navarre.rationale: Kingdom of Navarre 824-1620. Use Ourednik 1200 Navarre (pre-1234 dynastic union; later partition reduced it).

byzantine-late-1025.rationale: Middle Byzantine 843-1204. Replaced duplicate-of-Justinian polygon with HBM 1000 Byzantine Empire (~Basil II 1025 peak): Anatolia + Balkans + Crete + Cyprus + S Italy. Excludes the lost Italian/African western Justinianic territories.

kingdom-of-scotland.rationale: Scotland 843-1707. Replaced 15-vertex stub with Ourednik 1530 Scotland (mainland + Hebrides + Orkney).

kyivan-rus.rationale: Kievan Rus' 882-1240. Use Ourednik 1100 (peak under Vladimir Monomakh) — Novgorod to lower Dnieper, including Galicia–Volhynia, but not Suzdal–Vladimir hinterland yet of Moscow.

kingdom-of-england.rationale: England 927-1707 (pre-Acts of Union). Uses Ourednik 1500 (England before union with Ireland was formalised; Wales already incorporated 1284-1542).

holy-roman-empire.rationale: HRE at its medieval high under Hohenstaufen (Frederick II), encompassing Germany, Burgundy, N Italy and Bohemia. Replaced with Ourednik 1200 CE.

kingdom-of-france.rationale: Kingdom of France 987-1792. Use post-Hundred-Years-War (1500) hexagon. English Aquitaine excluded after 1453.

kingdom-of-hungary.rationale: Hungary 1000-1526 (Ottoman conquest at Mohács). Use Ourednik 1400 — full Carpathian basin including Croatia, Slavonia, Transylvania.

kingdom-of-aragon.rationale: Crown of Aragon 1035-1516. Use Ourednik 1492 Aragón including Catalonia, Valencia, Balearics, Sardinia, Sicily and Naples (Alfonso V conquered Naples 1442).

kingdom-of-castile.rationale: Castile 1065-1516. Current polygon was tiny N-Iberian stub. Use Ourednik 1500 Castille — includes Granada (annexed 1492), most of Iberian peninsula except Aragon/Portugal/Navarre.

europe-republic-of-genoa.rationale: Genoa 1099-1797. Use Ourednik 1530 — Liguria. Note: Corsica was Genoese 1284-1768 but is captured under "Corsica" in HBM 1100/1200. Black Sea trading colonies (Caffa) not in Ourednik but historically part of the maritime empire.

kingdom-of-jerusalem.rationale: Kingdom of Jerusalem 1099-1291. Current polygon (67 vtx, bbox [34.2,29.2,37.5,34.4]) covers the Levantine coastal strip from Gulf of Aqaba to the Lebanese coast, matching standard Cambridge/Wikipedia maps of the Crusader kingdom at the 1187 pre-Hattin maximum.

europe-florence.rationale: Republic/Duchy of Florence 1115-1569. Use Ourednik 1530 — Florentine Tuscany.

kingdom-of-portugal.rationale: Portugal 1139-1580 (Iberian Union begins 1580). Use Ourednik 1500 Portugal — modern Portuguese mainland.

europe-bulgarian-second.rationale: Second Bulgarian Empire 1185-1396. Use Ourednik 1300 Bulgar Khanate — most of modern Bulgaria + parts of Romanian plain + N Thrace.

latin-empire.rationale: Latin Empire of Constantinople 1204-1261. Per Partitio Romaniae (1204), the Latin Emperor held Thrace and parts of Bithynia plus a quarter of Constantinople; Frankish crusader vassal states (Thessalonica, Athens, Achaea, Euboea) controlled most of Greece. Hand-built MultiPolygon encompassing the imperial heartland and principal vassal principalities.

europe-naples.rationale: Kingdom of Naples 1282-1816 (post-Sicilian-Vespers). Use Ourednik 1530 — southern Italian peninsula.

grand-duchy-moscow.rationale: Grand Duchy of Moscow 1283-1547. Use Ourednik 1492 — post-Ivan III consolidation including Novgorod (1478), Tver (1485), Vyatka (1489).

swiss-confederation.rationale: Old Swiss Confederacy 1291-1848. Use Ourednik 1530 Thirteen Cantons (just after permanent admission of Basel/Schaffhausen/Appenzell).

europe-serbian-empire.rationale: Serbian Empire under Stefan Dušan, crowned Tsar 1346. At the 1355 peak the empire stretched from the Danube to the Gulf of Corinth, and from the Adriatic (Durrës) to the Maritsa river. Expanded the southern envelope down to ~lat 39.0 and east to ~lon 25.0 while keeping the northern Morava-valley shape.

kingdom-of-burgundy.rationale: Kingdom of Burgundy / Burgundian state. Note the entry name "Burgandy" 824-1378 (HBM typo). For Valois Burgundy (1363-1477) the Ourednik 1200 Burgandy approximates the core kingdom; later Valois additions in the Low Countries are not captured by HBM.

poland-lithuania.rationale: Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth 1386-1795 (Krewo 1386 → Lublin 1569). Peak ~1619. Use Ourednik 1600 (typo "Poland-Llituania" in source) — Poland + Belarus + most of Ukraine + Lithuania + Latvia.

europe-milan.rationale: Duchy of Milan 1395-1797. Use Ourednik 1530 — Lombardy.

kalmar-union.rationale: Kalmar Union 1397-1523. Uses Ourednik 1500 covering Denmark, Norway, Sweden + Norse Greenland and Iceland.

russian-empire.rationale: Russian Empire 1547-1917. Current polygon (vtx=7052, bbox crosses antimeridian, lat 35-82) matches the 1900 maximum extent in Ourednik HBM 1900. No correction needed.

dutch-republic.rationale: Dutch Republic 1581-1795 (Act of Abjuration → Batavian Republic). Use Ourednik 1700 — the Seven United Provinces. Overseas Dutch East/West Indies are separate polities.

swedish-empire.rationale: Stormaktstiden 1611-1721. Peak under Charles XII; Ourednik 1700 Sweden includes Finland, Estonia, Livonia, Ingria, Karelia, Pomerania, Bremen-Verden, Wismar.

egyptian-old-kingdom.rationale: Current geometry is the HBM 'Egypt' polygon for -2000, matching the Andrei Ourednik historical-basemaps reconstruction (Nile valley from the Mediterranean south to ~19.8N near the 2nd cataract). This is a reasonable representation of Old Kingdom Egypt's effective territorial extent (Egypt proper + Lower Nubia frontier under Sneferu/Pepi I). bbox=(29.36, 19.80, 33.74, 31.47) is consistent with canonical maps.

africa-kush-kingdom.rationale: Current 21-vertex polygon (29.1 to 36.0 lon, 13.8 to 22.7 lat) covers the Napatan-Meroitic Nile corridor and Butana steppe from first cataract (Aswan area) south to ~Khartoum. Matches HBM "Kush" -400 (30.2 to 34.6 lon, 16.1 to 23.5 lat) but extended south to include Meroe/Butana. Already marked dashed; canonical for Napatan/Meroitic c. 700 BCE - 350 CE.

africa-punt.rationale: Current 256-vertex MultiPolygon (36.42 to 48.94 lon, 8.00 to 18.00 lat) covers the Horn of Africa from Eritrea coast to N Somalia / Djibouti — matching modern scholarly consensus per Wikipedia and 2020 strontium-isotope study of mummified baboons placing Punt in modern Eritrea/Ethiopia/NW Somalia. Acceptable.

akkadian-empire.rationale: Current 141-vertex Polygon has bbox (37.0-49.0E, 29.1-37.0N), which matches the accepted Akkadian maximum extent under Naram-Sin: from Ebla/Mari in the west (~36-37E), Anatolian Taurus foothills (~37N), Zagros east, and the Persian Gulf south (~29N). World History Encyclopedia and Wikipedia maps consistently show this bbox. HBM has no Akkad polygon (closest analogue 'Ur' bc-2000 has bbox 40.8-50.1E, 29.3-35.7N, which is post-Akkadian Ur III and too small). Current geometry is reasonable; kept.

egyptian-middle-kingdom.rationale: Same HBM 'Egypt' polygon as Old Kingdom (bbox 29.36-33.74E, 19.80-31.47N). Middle Kingdom (Senusret III) extended south to the 2nd cataract / Semna fortresses (~21.5N), so 19.8N southern bound is slightly generous but within plausible reconstruction of nominal Egyptian sphere. Sinai mining outposts and some southern Levant contact also fit. Kept as HBM-canonical.

babylonian-hammurabi.rationale: Original 9-vertex polygon (bbox 44-49.45E, 31-34.69N) covered only southern Mesopotamia and omitted the cities Hammurabi explicitly claimed in his code prologue: Mari (40.9E, 34.5N), Tuttul on the Balikh, Eshnunna (44.7E, 33.6N), and nominally Assur (43.3E, 35.5N) and Nineveh (43.2E, 36.4N). Replaced with a 28-vertex polygon covering Lower Mesopotamia from the Persian Gulf, up the Euphrates to Mari and the Balikh confluence, across to the upper Tigris at Assur/Nineveh, and east into the Diyala valley to Eshnunna. Conforms to the bbox shown on Wikipedia's File:Hammurabi's Babylonia 1.svg and the World History Encyclopedia map of Babylon at Hammurabi's time.

hittite-empire.rationale: Current MultiPolygon (bbox 30.56-41.18E, 33.23-41.69N, 97 verts) is the HBM 'Hittites' polygon for -1500/-1000, which captures the empire's maximum extent under Suppiluliuma I/Mursili II: central Anatolia (Hattusa region) extending west to the Aegean, south to Kizzuwatna and northern Syria (Aleppo, Carchemish), and east to the upper Euphrates. Matches World History Encyclopedia map of Hittite Empire c.1300 BC. Kept.

asia-shang-dynasty.rationale: HBM has no Shang feature. Current bbox 108.5-119.3E, 30.6-39.2N covers middle/lower Yellow River basin (Henan + parts of Shanxi/Hebei/Shandong) which matches scholarly consensus on Shang oracle-bone era heartland. Boundary is dashed/uncertain because Shang control was diffuse and varied over the dynasty's 600+ years. Keep dashed; no canonical replacement available.

egyptian-new-kingdom-early.rationale: Current MultiPolygon (bbox 27.5-34.49E, 21.99-30.48N, 104 verts) covers Egypt proper plus Sinai with a slight eastward extension into southern Canaan, appropriate for early 18th Dynasty (Ahmose-Hatshepsut, 1550-1479 BC) before Thutmose III's Levantine conquests. The polygon does NOT yet include the Syrian empire, which is correct: Hyksos were driven out only to Sharuhen in southern Canaan, and Egypt's northern frontier was still close to Sinai. Kept.

mitanni-kingdom.rationale: Original 73-vertex polygon (bbox 36.01-42.99E, 34.51-38.49N) was a hand-drawn elliptical shape with a 'handle' artifact, and notably did NOT extend east to Nuzi/Kirkuk (~44.4E, 35.5N) or include Nineveh on the upper Tigris, which Shaushtatar's empire controlled per Wikipedia/World History Encyclopedia. Replaced with a 19-vertex polygon covering the Mediterranean coast (Alalakh ~36.4E), Aleppo, Khabur Triangle, upper Tigris to Nineveh, east through Erbil to Kirkuk/Nuzi (~45.5E), and south along the middle Euphrates to Mari. This is the canonical Hanigalbat/Mitanni extent c.1430 BC under Shaushtatar.

egyptian-new-kingdom-peak.rationale: Original used HBM 'Egypt' -1500 polygon (bbox 29.36-33.74E, 22.68-31.47N), which is ONLY core Egypt and omits the entire Asian empire that defines this period (1479-1200 BC, Thutmose III through Ramesses II). Per Britannica/Wikipedia, under Thutmose III Egypt reached the Euphrates near Carchemish (~38E, 36.8N) and south to the 4th cataract (~32E, 18.5N). After Kadesh (1274 BC), the northern frontier with the Hittites was set near Kadesh on the Orontes (~36.6E, 34.6N). Replaced with a 37-vertex polygon covering Egypt + Sinai + Canaan + coastal Phoenicia + inland Syria-Palestine to Kadesh/Carchemish + Lower Nubia/Kush to 4th cataract + western oases. bbox=(25.5-38.0E, 18.5-36.8N).

assyrian-middle.rationale: Current 12-vertex Polygon (bbox 40.79-46.11E, 33.32-37.81N) matches the HBM 'Assyria' polygon for -1500/-1000 exactly, representing the Assyrian heartland (Assur-Nineveh-Arbil triangle and Khabur basin). Middle Assyrian Empire at its peak under Tukulti-Ninurta I (1233-1197 BC) briefly controlled Babylon and reached further south, so the polygon arguably underrepresents the true maximum. The dashed/accurate=false flagging is appropriate for the heartland-only interpretation. Kept at current accuracy level.

egyptian-new-kingdom-late.rationale: Same HBM 'Egypt' -1000 polygon as the NK-peak (bbox 29.36-33.74E, 22.68-31.47N), showing only core Egypt. For the 1200-1070 BC late Ramesside period this is partially correct (empire was contracting), but the boundaries shifted dramatically across this 130-year window: Ramesses III still held parts of Canaan in the early 12th century and Ramesses IX's cartouche has been found at Gezer, while by 1070 BC essentially all foreign territory was lost. A single solid polygon misrepresents this dynamic. Downgraded to dashed/accurate=false to signal the period's shifting frontiers; geometry retained as end-of-period snapshot.

carthaginian-empire.rationale: Current polygon (249 verts, bbox -7.5,29.5,25.2,41.0) is a modern-country reconstruction extending east into the Libyan desert that was never Carthaginian.  Replaced with HBM bc500 "Carthaginian Empire" feature (232 verts, bbox -7.2,29.8,19.1,41.2): North African coastal strip, Sardinia, Sicily, southern Iberia at pre-First-Punic-War peak.

achaemenid-persian-empire.rationale: Current 1071-vertex geometry is a modern-country reconstruction; correct extent but anachronistic borders. Replaced with HBM bc500 "Achaemenid Empire" (534 verts) covering Darius I peak: Indus Valley, Egypt/Nubia, Thrace, Aegean coast, Caucasus.

macedonian-alexander.rationale: Current geometry is identical (same hash) to the Achaemenid polygon — both were modern-country reconstructions.  Replaced with HBM bc323 "Empire of Alexander" (738 verts) representing Alexander's extent at his death: Macedonia + former Achaemenid lands (Egypt, Persia, Bactria, Indus Valley).

seleucid-empire.rationale: Current 462-vertex polygon (bbox 29-75E, 25-43N) is a modern-country reconstruction that wrongly extends east into Bactria/Sogdia (broke away under Diodotus by 250 BC). Replaced with HBM bc200 "Seleucid Kingdom" (226 verts, bbox 26-61E, 25.5-40.5N) — Antiochus III early peak.

ptolemaic-egypt.rationale: Current polygon (bbox 16-37E, 22-35N) is mostly modern Egypt + eastern Libya — misses Ptolemaic possessions of Cyprus, Coele-Syria and southern Anatolia.  Replaced with HBM bc200 "Ptolemaic Kingdom" feature (335 verts) which includes Cyrenaica, Cyprus, coastal Levant.

roman-republic-early.rationale: Current polygon covers ONLY Italy + Sicily (bbox 9-17E, 37-47N) but by 133 BC the Republic also controlled Sardinia, Corsica, Hispania Citerior/Ulterior, and Africa province (146 BC).  Replaced with HBM bc200 "Rome" (407 verts, bbox -7-21E, 36-47N): Italy + Sicily + Sardinia + Corsica + Iberian coast.

parthian-empire.rationale: Current 97-vertex polygon matches HBM year 100 "Parthian Empire" exactly.  Extent (Euphrates to Hindu Kush, Caspian to Persian Gulf) corresponds to Vologases I era and is broadly correct.  Kept; source string upgraded to historical-basemaps.

asia-khotan.rationale: Current 18-vertex hand-traced polygon (76.5-86.7E, 36.5-38.7N) covers the Khotan oasis-chain along the southern Tarim from Kashgar to Niya.  Matches Stein documentation.  Border switched to dashed since Tarim oasis kingdoms had fuzzy frontiers.

asia-nabataean.rationale: Replaced 97-vertex modern-country polygon with HBM 100 "Nabatean Kingdom" feature (47 verts, 32.4-38.5E, 26.7-32N) — Aretas IV peak ~9 BC-40 AD.

roman-republic-late.rationale: Current polygon (2179 verts, bbox -17 to 43E, 19 to 56.5N) is a modern-country reconstruction covering Scotland and the Sahara — neither was Roman.  Replaced with the union of both HBM bc100 "Roman Republic" features (Asia province + main Republic), ~850 verts, covering Iberia south of Cantabria, Gallia Narbonensis, Italy, Greece, Asia Minor west coast, Cyrenaica, NW Africa coast.

roman-empire-augustus.rationale: Current geometry hashes identically to HBM year 100 — i.e. it is Trajan-era Rome including Dacia, Mesopotamia, and Britain, none of which Augustus controlled.  Replaced with HBM bc1 "Roman Empire" (1496 verts) matching Augustus's final extent: Iberia, Gaul, Italy, Balkans, Asia Minor, Levant, Egypt, North Africa; NO Britain, NO Dacia, NO Mesopotamia.

roman-empire-trajan.rationale: Current geometry equals HBM year 100 "Roman Empire" (1579 verts, bbox -9.55-48.27E, 22.7-54.9N) — the standard map of the Empire at Trajan's death: Britain to Hadrian's Wall, Iberia, Gaul, Italy, Dacia (added 106), Asia Minor, Mesopotamia (briefly held), Syria, Arabia Petraea, Egypt, North Africa.  Kept; source upgraded to historical-basemaps.

roman-empire-late.rationale: Current polygon (2150 verts, 56.4N to 19N, -17E to 42E) is a modern-country reconstruction including Sahara and Scotland which were not Roman.  Replaced with HBM year 200 "Roman Empire" (1625 verts, bbox -9.55-48.27E, 22.7-54.9N) — Severan-era extent matching the typical "post-180 stable empire" Britannica/Shepherd map.

asia-pyu-city-states.rationale: Current 228-vertex polygon (93-99E, 15.7-23N) covers most of modern Myanmar including Mon and Arakanese regions never Pyu.  Pyu city-states (Halin, Beikthano, Sri Ksetra) occupied the central Irrawaddy valley from roughly 16.5N (Pyay) to 22.5N (Halin).  Replaced with 12-vertex hand-traced polygon; dashed border because Pyu was a loose city-state network.

sassanid-empire.rationale: Current geometry is catastrophically wrong: bbox 41.2-52.4E, 12.6-19.2N is the SOUTHERN ARABIAN PENINSULA (Yemen / Hadhramaut), not Sasanian territory at all.  The Sasanian Empire occupied Iran, Iraq, the Caucasus, parts of Central Asia, eastern Arabian coast (Oman) and at peak briefly Egypt/Anatolia.  Replaced with hand-traced 24-vertex polygon for the Khosrow II peak ~620 AD per Wikipedia "Sasanian Empire at greatest extent".

western-roman-empire.rationale: Current 115-vertex polygon (-9.55 to 20.71E, 29.4-52.1N) covers Iberia, Gaul, Italy, parts of Illyricum, NW African provinces.  Matches the standard 395-410 Western Roman extent.  Britain still nominally Western pre-410.  Kept as reasonable approximation.

huari-empire.rationale: Replaced current 95-vertex polygon with HBM 700 "Huari Empire" feature for consistency with dataset.  Both have similar extents along the Peruvian central highlands.

republic-of-venice.rationale: Current 114-vertex polygon (9.5-17.3E, 43.1-47.1N) covers the Domini di Terraferma (Veneto + Friuli + Istria + Dalmatian coast) ~1500.  Stato da Mar (Crete, Cyprus, Ionian Islands, Morea) is not included — known limitation given those territories were acquired/lost at different dates.  Kept as European-core approximation.

spanish-americas.rationale: Current 3894-vertex polygon (-118 to -53E, -56 to 33N) captures the Americas core (viceroyalties of New Spain, Peru, New Granada, Rio de la Plata) at near-peak ~1790.  Missing California, Florida, Philippines — but the Americas core is correctly bounded.  Kept.

portuguese-brazil.rationale: Current 1026-vertex polygon (-74 to -35E, -34 to 5N) matches modern Brazil, which is roughly Portuguese Brazil post-Treaty-of-Madrid (1750) and Treaty of San Ildefonso (1777).  Pre-1750 Brazil was smaller (Tordesillas line at 46W).  Kept as ~1800 approximation.

british-empire-1700.rationale: British Isles + Atlantic seaboard colonies + Caribbean + Hudson Bay Company forts (chartered 1670).  Bbox -79 to 1.75E, 17.7-60.6N matches Wikipedia "First British Empire" pre-Seven-Years-War.  Current geometry uses clipped modern-country borders, which is reasonable for post-1700 colonial jurisdictions that broadly anticipate modern borders.  Kept.

british-empire-1750.rationale: Expanded Hudson Bay claims, all 13 colonies developed, but pre-Seven-Years-War — France still held Canada.  Bbox -115 to 1.75E, 17.7-70N reflects expanded Rupert's Land.  Current geometry uses clipped modern-country borders, which is reasonable for post-1700 colonial jurisdictions that broadly anticipate modern borders.  Kept.

british-empire-1763.rationale: Post-Treaty of Paris (1763): all of New France ceded to Britain.  Bbox -141 to 92.6E, 17.7-83N includes Canada to Pacific, Caribbean (Grenada, Tobago), Bengal/Madras/Bombay post-Plassey.  Current geometry uses clipped modern-country borders, which is reasonable for post-1700 colonial jurisdictions that broadly anticipate modern borders.  Kept.

british-empire-1783.rationale: Post-Treaty of Paris (1783): lost 13 American colonies but retained Canada, Caribbean, India footholds; Cook voyages added Pacific.  Bbox -141 to 92.6E, 15.9-83N.  Current geometry uses clipped modern-country borders, which is reasonable for post-1700 colonial jurisdictions that broadly anticipate modern borders.  Kept.

german-east-africa.rationale: Current 30-vertex polygon (28.8-40.5E, -11.8 to -1.1N) matches German East Africa: Tanganyika + Rwanda + Burundi.  Upgraded "accurate" flag from false to true after verification against Wikipedia "German East Africa" map.

korean-empire.rationale: Current 456-vertex polygon (124.3-130.7E, 33.2-43N) covers the Korean peninsula.  The Daehan Jeguk (1897-1910) controlled the entire peninsula, so a modern-country reconstruction is appropriate.  Kept.

asia-zhou-dynasty.rationale: Current geometry MD5 a199e99cb5 matches HBM Zhou_-500 'Zhou states' exactly. bbox 104.3-122.4E, 27.1-40.4N covers the Spring & Autumn / Warring States era Zhou-recognized polities along the Yellow and middle Yangtze basins.

qin-dynasty.rationale: Original geometry stopped at ~28.5N south, missing the Lingnan conquest (Guangdong/Guangxi/N. Vietnam) completed in 214 BCE. Replacement extends south to ~21N to include Nanhai/Guilin/Xiang commanderies, while keeping the western boundary at ~102E (Sichuan) and not extending into Tarim/Tibet/Mongolia as required. Border kept dashed because southern frontier was newly conquered and tenuous.

han-dynasty-china.rationale: Current geometry matches HBM Han_100 exactly (MD5 9b1dcba8da). bbox 94.6-126.2E, 17.7-42.7N includes Tarim Basin (Western Regions) at western edge ~94E, Jiaozhi (Vietnam) at southern edge ~17.7N, Lelang in Korean peninsula at northeast, and Mongolian frontier at ~42.7N - matches Eastern Han peak extent.

asia-silla.rationale: Original bbox 126.1-130.9E, 33.2-38.6N truncates Unified Silla's northern extent. After 668 CE Silla unified the peninsula south of the Taedong River (~39N). Replacing with HBM Silla_700 (bbox 124.7-129.6E, 34.8-39.1N) which is the canonical Ourednik Unified Silla extent.

asia-goguryeo.rationale: Current bbox 121.0-130.7E, 37.0-45.0N correctly extends into modern NE China (Liaoning/Jilin) and the northern Korean peninsula - matches Goguryeo's 5th-6th c peak extent. Western reach to 121E covers Liaodong; northern reach to 45N covers Jilin/Heilongjiang frontier; doesn't extend south of 37N (correctly excludes southern peninsula held by Baekje/Silla).

goguryeo-kingdom.rationale: Original geometry bbox 125.7-129.6E, 37.1-43.0N only covered the northern Korean peninsula, missing Goguryeo's extensive Liaoning/Jilin holdings in modern NE China. Replacing with the broader asia-goguryeo geometry (bbox 121-130.7E, 37-45N) which correctly includes Liaodong peninsula and Jilin frontier per historical record of Goguryeo's 5th-6th c. peak.

asia-baekje-kingdom.rationale: Current bbox 126.1-128.0E, 33.2-38.3N covers SW Korean peninsula (modern Chungcheong + Jeolla + S. Gyeonggi) which matches Baekje's territory before Silla absorption in 660 CE. Border dashed because Baekje borders with Silla and Goguryeo shifted continually over its 700-year existence.

asia-three-kingdoms.rationale: Current bbox 98.8-122.7E, 22.6-41.8N covers Wei (north) + Shu (Sichuan/Yunnan west) + Wu (southeast) combined extent during the 220-280 CE period. Correctly excludes the Western Regions/Tarim (lost by Cao Wei after Han collapse) and northern Mongolia. HBM lacks a Three Kingdoms feature.

asia-jin-dynasty.rationale: Current geometry matches HBM Jin_300 exactly (MD5 bd1c4e91f3). bbox 94.6-126.2E, 17.7-42.7N is identical to Han peak extent - Western Jin briefly re-unified China and held the Han territories before the 4 c. fragmentation.

asia-chera-dynasty.rationale: Current geometry covers Kerala and western Tamil Nadu (75-78E, 8-13N) — appropriate for Chera/Kerala kingdom extent. Matches HBM 'Cheras' polygons across 500-700 CE in shape & position.

asia-yamato-kingdom.rationale: Original geometry bbox 133-137E, 33.1-36.3N covered only Shikoku and a sliver of central Honshu - grossly understates Yamato's reach. By the 6th-7th c. Yamato controlled most of Honshu south of Tohoku plus Shikoku and N. Kyushu. Replacing with HBM Yamato_600 (bbox 129.3-141.0E, 30.9-38.3N) which is the canonical Ourednik Yamato Japan extent.

asia-northern-southern-dynasties.rationale: Current geometry matches HBM Toba Wei_500 exactly (MD5 923c0521fb). bbox 96.3-124.7E, 33.1-43.1N captures the Northern Wei extent at 500 CE which dominated the Northern Dynasties era. (HBM has no single feature for the combined Northern + Southern dynasties.)

sui-dynasty.rationale: Current geometry matches HBM Sui_600 exactly (MD5 4dc5670188). bbox 96.4-124.7E, 16.2-43.1N reflects Sui re-unification including the southern dynasties' Yangtze/Lingnan territory back to Vietnam (~16N).

tang-dynasty.rationale: Current geometry matches HBM Tang_800 exactly (MD5 29afe28de8). bbox 102.4-126.0E, 16.2-43.0N reflects post-An Lushan Tang (after loss of Western Regions to Tibetan and Uyghur expansion). NOTE: HBM Tang understates the pre-755 peak which included the Tarim Basin and parts of Central Asia via the Protectorates - but using the HBM canonical 800 CE extent as required.

asia-heian-period.rationale: Original geometry bbox 133.0-137.0E, 33.2-36.7N covered only Shikoku/central Honshu - identical to incorrect Yamato/Kamakura/Ashikaga geometry. Replacing with HBM Imperial Japan (Fujiwara)_1100 (bbox 129.3-142.0E, 30.9-41.4N) which is the canonical Ourednik Heian-era Japan including all Honshu, Shikoku, Kyushu and reaching into northern Honshu (Tohoku). Correctly excludes Hokkaido.

asia-goryeo.rationale: Original bbox extends to 43N - too far north. Goryeo's stable northern border was the Yalu / Cheollima Line (~41-42N). Replacing with HBM Goryeo_1200 (bbox 124.1-130.9E, 33.2-41.9N) which is the canonical Ourednik Goryeo at peak.

asia-song-northern.rationale: Current geometry matches HBM Song_1000 exactly (MD5 a898682920). bbox 100.5-122.4E, 20.2-39.9N reflects Northern Song extent (excluding Liao-held Sixteen Prefectures north of ~40N, and Xixia in the NW). Correctly does not include Mongolia, Tarim or Tibet.

song-dynasty-northern.rationale: Current geometry matches HBM Song_1000 exactly (MD5 a898682920). bbox 100.5-122.4E, 20.2-39.9N reflects Northern Song extent (excluding Liao-held Sixteen Prefectures north of ~40N, and Xixia in the NW). Correctly does not include Mongolia, Tarim or Tibet.

asia-tangut-western-xia.rationale: Geometry already matches HBM Xixia_1000 exactly (MD5 229d2351b5) - bbox 85.1-110.5E, 37.7-42.1N captures Tangut Western Xia heartland in the Ordos/Gansu/Qinghai corridor. Previous metadata flagged accurate=false dashed, but the geometry is the canonical Ourednik feature, so upgrade to accurate=true solid.

asia-song-southern.rationale: Current geometry matches HBM Song_1200 exactly (MD5 20f072fa32). After 1127 loss of north China to Jurchen Jin, Southern Song retained Yangtze basin and southern half of the country. NOTE: HBM's Song_1200 polygon still uses the full Northern Song extent in this file (HBM doesn't appear to redraw to the actual Southern Song southern half), which is a HBM limitation - but as the canonical source we must follow it.

song-dynasty-southern.rationale: BUG: original geometry MD5 a898682920 was the Northern Song HBM 1000 feature, not Southern Song. Both song-dynasty-northern and song-dynasty-southern shared the Northern Song geometry. Replacing with HBM Song_1200 (MD5 20f072fa32) matching the parallel asia-song-southern entry.

asia-kakatiya-dynasty.rationale: Current bbox (77.0-82.8E, 12.0-20.0N) covers Telangana/coastal Andhra — appropriate Kakatiya extent under Ganapati & Rudrama.

asia-kamakura-shogunate.rationale: Original geometry bbox 133.0-137.0E, 33.2-36.7N covered only Shikoku and central Honshu - identical to incorrect Heian/Yamato/Ashikaga geometry. Replacing with HBM Shogun Japan (Kamakura)_1300 (bbox 129.3-142.0E, 30.9-41.4N) including all of Honshu, Shikoku, Kyushu but excluding Hokkaido (correct - Ezo/Hokkaido was Ainu territory not under Kamakura control).

asia-yadava-dynasty.rationale: Current bbox (72.5-79.5E, 15.5-22.0N) covers Maharashtra/north Karnataka — appropriate Seuna Yadava extent under Singhana/Ramachandra.

asia-ashikaga-shogunate.rationale: Original geometry bbox 133.0-137.0E, 33.2-36.7N covered only Shikoku and central Honshu - identical to incorrect Yamato/Heian/Kamakura geometry. Replacing with HBM Shogun Japan_1400 (bbox 129.3-142.0E, 30.9-41.4N) which represents the Ashikaga (Muromachi) shogunate extent: all Honshu, Shikoku, Kyushu; correctly excludes Hokkaido (Ezo/Ainu lands).

asia-ming-dynasty.rationale: Current geometry matches HBM Ming Chinese Empire_1500 exactly (MD5 a816b9f2ba). bbox 95.2-131.9E, 19.7-43.3N includes the core 15-province Ming territory plus Liaodong/Nurgan in Manchuria. Correctly does NOT include Mongolia (Northern Yuan / Oirats), Xinjiang (Moghulistan), or Tibet (Phagmodrupa) - those came under Qing only.

ming-dynasty-1400.rationale: Current geometry matches HBM Ming Chinese Empire_1500 exactly (MD5 a816b9f2ba). bbox 95.2-131.9E, 19.7-43.3N includes the core 15-province Ming territory plus Liaodong/Nurgan in Manchuria. Correctly does NOT include Mongolia (Northern Yuan / Oirats), Xinjiang (Moghulistan), or Tibet (Phagmodrupa) - those came under Qing only.

joseon-dynasty.rationale: Original was a reconstructed-clipped-country approximation. Replacing with HBM Korea_1800 (bbox 124.1-130.9E, 33.2-43.0N) which is the canonical Ourednik Joseon-era Korea covering the full peninsula north to the Yalu/Tumen.

asia-ryukyu-kingdom.rationale: Original geometry bbox 127.6-128.3E, 26.1-26.9N covered only Okinawa main island. After unification by Sho Hashi (1429) the Ryukyu Kingdom controlled the full Ryukyu archipelago: Amami group (north, ~28-28.5N - lost to Satsuma 1609), Okinawa group (central), Miyako and Yaeyama (south, to ~24N). Replacement uses 4-island-group MultiPolygon spanning 123.7-129.8E, 24.2-28.5N. Border kept dashed because Ryukyu was archipelagic - the polygon envelopes are not contiguous land.

asia-sengoku-ashikaga.rationale: Original geometry was identical to Tokugawa (bbox 123.7-145.8E, 24.3-45.5N) - that includes all of Hokkaido and the Ryukyu archipelago, neither of which was part of Sengoku-era Japan (Ezo/Hokkaido was Ainu territory until Matsumae 1604; Ryukyu was an independent kingdom until 1609). Replacing with HBM Japan (Warring States)_1530 (bbox 129.3-142.0E, 30.9-41.4N) which correctly limits Sengoku Japan to Honshu+Shikoku+Kyushu.

tokugawa-shogunate.rationale: Original bbox 123.7-145.8E, 24.3-45.5N included Ryukyu archipelago southern islands (Yaeyama at 24N), which were part of the Ryukyu Kingdom not Tokugawa Japan proper (Ryukyu became a Satsuma vassal in 1609 but retained sovereignty until 1879). Replacing with HBM Japan_1783 (bbox 129.3-145.4E, 30.9-45.4N) which correctly excludes Ryukyu and reflects late Tokugawa extent including Matsumae's tip of Hokkaido. HBM does over-include all of Hokkaido (Ainu Ezo was largely independent until Meiji) but as the canonical source we follow it.

qing-dynasty-1790.rationale: Original was a reconstructed-clipped country approximation (bbox 74.1-141.3E, 20.2-56.9N, area 1293.8). Replacing with HBM Qing Empire_1800 (bbox 74.1-141.3E, 18.1-56.9N, area 1297.1) - canonical Ourednik Qing peak including Manchuria (NE), Mongolia (N), Xinjiang/Dzungaria (NW), Tibet (W), inner China, Taiwan, and the southern coast.

asia-qing-peak.rationale: Original (bbox 73.6-134.8E, 18.2-53.6N, area 1138.8) closely matched HBM Manchu Empire_1815 but with eastern bound truncated to 134.8E - that under-represents Qing peak's hold on Outer Manchuria (Russian Far East coast to ~141E, ceded 1860 in Treaty of Aigun/Peking). Replacing with HBM Qing Empire_1800 (bbox 74.1-141.3E, 18.1-56.9N) which is the canonical 1800 (peak era) feature and correctly extends to the Sea of Okhotsk coast.

asia-maurya.rationale: Current geometry extends south to ~8N (Cape Comorin), including Chera/Chola/Pandya territories which Maurya never controlled. Per Schwartzberg and HBM, Ashoka's peak (~250 BCE) reached ~14N (south of Krishna), excluding the deep Tamil south. Replaced with HBM Mauryan Empire @ 200 BCE.

gupta-empire.rationale: Current geometry is clipped to modern India (eastern extent stops at ~91E, missing Bangladesh/Brahmaputra valley which was Gupta territory). HBM Gupta@400 includes proper eastern reach to ~94E and northern reach to ~34N (with vassal extension into central Deccan, consistent with Chandragupta II era).

kushan-empire.rationale: OUT-OF-SCOPE for the Africa subset: the Kushan Empire was a Bactrian / N Indian polity, not African. This entry was mis-grouped in africa.json subset. Current polygon (60.49 to 82.26 lon, 23.69 to 41.04 lat) covers the canonical Kushan extent (Bactria + Gandhara + N Indian plain) and is acceptable in its own right — defer to central_asia_steppe or south_southeast_asia audit.

asia-pandya-empire.rationale: Current bbox (76.25-79.64E, 8.08-11.98N) covers far southern Tamil Nadu — appropriate Pandya core (Madurai region). HBM 'Pandya state'@1300 has matching extent.

asia-chola-empire.rationale: Current bbox (75.44-81.87E, 5.93-15.77N) — includes Tamil Nadu, southern Karnataka, Andhra coast and northern Sri Lanka — matches HBM 'Chola state'@1000 exactly. Appropriate for Rajaraja/Rajendra peak.

chola-dynasty.rationale: Duplicate of asia-chola-empire with the same canonical Chola@1000 extent. Mark accurate=true to match.

asia-hoysala-empire.rationale: Current bbox (73.3-78.0E, 11.1-17.0N) covers southern Karnataka — appropriate Hoysala extent under Veera Ballala II/III.

asia-pala-empire.rationale: Current bbox (84.0-93.4E, 19.6-27.2N) matches HBM 'Palas'@800-900 exactly — Bengal, Bihar, Odisha core. Appropriate for Dharmapala/Devapala peak.

asia-bahmani-sultanate.rationale: Current geometry has near-zero area (degenerate). Replaced with approximate polygon covering Bahmani extent at peak (late 15th c): northern Karnataka + Telangana + south Maharashtra (excluding Konkan coast), bounded by Krishna river to the south and Tapti to the north. Border kept dashed since territorial control was fluid.

asia-deccan-sultanate-bijapur.rationale: Current bbox (73.2-78.0E, 12.0-18.0N) — south Maharashtra + N Karnataka, extending south after annexing Vijayanagara territories post-1565. Appropriate Bijapur extent under Ibrahim Adil Shah II / Muhammad Adil Shah.

asia-deccan-sultanate-ahmadnagar.rationale: Current geometry extends too far south (to 14N — overlaps Bijapur/Vijayanagara zone) and not far enough north. HBM Ahmadnagar@1600 (72.8-78.6E, 16.6-23.9N) covers proper Nizam Shahi extent: Khandesh, west Berar, Maharashtra interior down to Bhima river.

asia-deccan-sultanate-golconda.rationale: Current bbox (77.0-81.0E, 14.0-20.0N) is too narrow — Golconda after 1565 expanded east to the Bay of Bengal and south into Vijayanagara remnants (Karnatak-Payanghat). HBM Golkonda@1650 (77.3-84.3E, 11.7-19.2N) properly covers coastal Andhra and the Tamil south extensions under Abdullah Qutb Shah.

delhi-sultanate.rationale: Current bbox (64.6-91.5E, 12.5-37.0N) appropriate for peak under Muhammad bin Tughluq (~1330) — extended from Punjab to Bengal, briefly to Madurai. HBM 'Sultanate of Delhi'@1400 has similar peak extent.

vijayanagara-empire.rationale: Current bbox (73.49-80.46E, 8.05-16.31N) matches HBM 'Vijayanagara'@1500 exactly — covers Karnataka, Andhra south of Krishna, Tamil Nadu down to Cape Comorin. Appropriate for Krishnadevaraya peak.

asia-maratha-confederacy.rationale: Current geometry extends south to 8.13N (Madurai/Cape Comorin), which the Marathas never controlled directly. HBM Maratha Confederacy@1800 (68.9-86.9E, 14.3-26.5N) is the appropriate confederation extent. Border dashed to reflect loose confederation structure with multiple chiefdoms (Peshwa, Scindia, Holkar, Bhonsle, Gaekwad).

maratha-empire.rationale: Current bbox (68.9-86.9E, 14.3-26.5N) matches HBM Maratha Confederacy@1800 exactly — appropriate extent of the loose confederation circa 1800. Mark accurate=true.

british-india-1765.rationale: Current bbox (81.0-92.6E, 19.1-26.9N) — Bengal, Bihar, Odisha (Diwani granted 1765). Appropriate for the territorial holdings of the East India Company after Buxar.

british-india.rationale: Current bbox (60.8-101.0E, 8.0-37.0N) matches HBM British Raj@1938 — covers entire subcontinent (modern Pakistan + India + Bangladesh + Burma) plus Aden. Per audit guidance, British India should not exclude Pakistan/Bangladesh — they were ALL British India until 1947. Current geometry is correct.

british-india-1805.rationale: Current bbox (72.7-92.6E, 8.2-27.7N) corresponds to post-Second Anglo-Maratha War extent: Bengal, Bihar, Madras, ceded districts of Andhra, parts of UP/Bundelkhand. Matches HBM British East India Company@1815 closely.

british-india-1850.rationale: Current bbox (66.0-89.0E, 7.0-36.0N) covers Company-ruled India in 1850 — post Sindh (1843) and Punjab (1849) annexations, before Lower Burma (1852) and 1857 mutiny. Reasonable extent. Mark accurate=true.

asia-funan.rationale: Current bbox (102.7-108.0E, 9.1-13.5N) covers southern Cambodia + Mekong delta — Funan's core. HBM 'Funan'@500-600 has similar extent.

asia-champa.rationale: Current bbox (106.1-109.5E, 10.0-16.8N) — central Vietnam coastal strip. Matches HBM 'Champa'@1000 exactly. Appropriate for the Cham polities along Annamese coast.

asia-srivijaya.rationale: Current bbox (95.2-111.3E, -7.9 to 8.9) covers Sumatra + Malay peninsula + western Java + western Borneo coast — appropriate Srivijaya maritime polity extent per audit guidance. Border kept dashed since Srivijaya was a thalassocracy with fluid tributary relationships, not a contiguous land empire.

srivijaya-empire.rationale: Duplicate of asia-srivijaya with same geometry. Mark accurate=true; border kept dashed for maritime polity.

khmer-empire.rationale: Current bbox (98.5-109.0E, 9.0-19.0N) — covers Cambodia, central/southern Thailand, southern Laos, southern Vietnam — matches audit guidance for Khmer peak under Jayavarman VII (~1200). Also matches HBM 'Khmer Empire'@1200 closely.

asia-pagan-kingdom.rationale: Current bbox (92.3-99.9E, 14.2-24.2N) covers Burma proper plus Tai-Shan frontier — appropriate Pagan extent under Narathihapate.

asia-bagan-kingdom.rationale: Synonym of Pagan Kingdom. Current bbox (93.0-97.0E, 16.0-26.0N) covers central Burma — appropriate Bagan core.

pagan-kingdom.rationale: Duplicate of asia-pagan-kingdom — current bbox (92.2-99.0E, 16.0-26.0N) is appropriate. Keep as-is.

asia-sukhothai-kingdom.rationale: Current bbox (98.1-102.0E, 12.0-20.0N) covers north-central Thailand. Appropriate Sukhothai core under Ramkhamhaeng (~1300). HBM 'Sukhothai'@1300 extends further (97.6-105.9E, 8.2-20.5N) with claimed tributaries — current core extent is reasonable.

ayutthaya-kingdom.rationale: Current bbox extends south to 3.23N (deep Malay peninsula past Kedah/Kelantan), which Ayutthaya only had nominal suzerainty over — direct rule did not reach that far. HBM 'Ayutthaya'@1700 (98.1-106.1E, 5.5-18.4N) represents the controlled extent: central Thailand plus northern Malay tributaries.

asia-lan-na-kingdom.rationale: Current bbox (97.4-101.0E, 15.0-20.5N) covers northern Thailand around Chiang Mai. Matches HBM 'Lan Na'@1600-1700 closely.

asia-lan-xang-kingdom.rationale: Current bbox (100.0-106.0E, 11.6-22.5N) covers Laos plus parts of NE Thailand and northern Cambodia border — appropriate Lan Xang extent under Sourigna Vongsa. HBM 'Laotian states'@1700 has similar reach.

asia-majapahit.rationale: Current bbox extends to 133E (West Papua) and -10.27S — claiming the entire 'Nusantara' suzerainty extent per Nagarakretagama. Per audit guidance, Majapahit's controlled core was eastern Java + Bali + parts of Sumatra. Replaced with core polygon: East/Central Java + Bali + Madura + Lombok + southern Sumatra (Palembang/Jambi tribute) + southern Borneo (Banjarmasin tribute). Border dashed to reflect tributary nature.

asia-malacca-sultanate.rationale: Current bbox (98.7-104.9E, -2.3 to 6.5N) covers Malay peninsula + east Sumatra coast (Riau, Indragiri tributaries). Appropriate for Malacca Sultanate pre-1511 Portuguese conquest. HBM 'Malacca'@1500 similar.

asia-aceh-sultanate.rationale: Current bbox (95.3-99.5E, 2.1-5.5N) — northern Sumatra. At Aceh's peak under Iskandar Muda (~1640), claimed control extended along west Sumatra coast and parts of Malay peninsula (Pahang/Kedah tributaries), but core was northern Sumatra. Border kept dashed; mark accurate=true for this conservative core extent.

asia-mataram-sultanate.rationale: Current bbox (107.8-114.7E, -8.5 to -5.7) covers central and eastern Java (excluding far west). Appropriate for Sultan Agung's Mataram (~1640).

asia-brunei-sultanate.rationale: Current bbox (114.0-116.0E, 2.1-5.6N) covers modern Brunei + Sarawak/Sabah coast. Brunei's 16th-century peak claimed much of Borneo + Sulu + parts of Mindanao/Luzon, but by 1800 the realm had contracted to this core. Border kept dashed.

asia-sultanate-sulu.rationale: Current bbox (119.1-122.6E, 5.1-8.1N) covers Sulu Archipelago + west Mindanao + north Borneo (Sabah claim). Appropriate Sulu Sultanate extent. Border kept dashed.

asia-sultanate-maguindanao.rationale: Current bbox (119.8-123.0E, 5.1-8.2N) covers western/central Mindanao + Cotabato basin. Appropriate Maguindanao Sultanate extent. Border kept dashed.

asia-konbaung-burma.rationale: Current bbox (92.2-101.2E, 9.8-28.5N) covers all of modern Myanmar + Manipur + Assam + Arakan + Tenasserim + parts of northern Thailand — appropriate Konbaung peak (~1820 pre-First Anglo-Burmese War).

dai-viet-vietnam.rationale: Current geometry extends south to 8.6N (Mekong delta), which Dai Viet (Ly/Tran dynasties, 1054-1400) did NOT control — Cochinchina south of Hue was Champa until late 15th c and Khmer until 17th c. HBM 'Đại Việt'@1300 (101.6-107.5E, 14.5-21.9N) represents the proper Tonkin + northern Annam extent.

asia-nguyen-vietnam.rationale: Current bbox (102.1-109.5E, 8.6-23.4N) covers unified Vietnam (Tonkin + Annam + Cochinchina, including Mekong delta absorbed from Khmer/Champa earlier). Appropriate for Nguyen Dynasty from 1802 under Gia Long/Minh Mang.

siam-rattanakosin.rationale: Current bbox (97.3-105.4E, 5.5-24.2N) covers Thailand + Laos vassals + western Cambodia + northern Malay tributaries. Appropriate for early/mid Rattanakosin peak (Rama I–III, before 1893 French losses). Mark accurate=true.

dutch-east-indies.rationale: Current bbox (95.2-141.0E, -10.9 to 5.7) covers full Indonesian archipelago plus West Papua. Matches HBM 'Netherlands Indies'@1914 — appropriate for the colony's full extent before independence.

spanish-philippines.rationale: Current bbox (117.2-126.6E, 5.6-18.6N) covers main Philippine archipelago. Matches HBM 'Philippines'@1800. Note: Spanish did not effectively control Muslim Mindanao/Sulu until late 19th c, but the nominal colony covered the archipelago.

kilwa-sultanate.rationale: Listed in south_southeast_asia subset but is actually a Swahili coast (East Africa) polity. Current bbox (38.5-40.2E, -11.0 to -6.0) covers Tanzanian coast / Kilwa Kisiwani area — appropriate. Audit unchanged.

africa-ghana-empire.rationale: Current 14-vertex polygon covers the Mauritania-Mali Sahel core (lon -12.5 to -3.9, lat 12.9 to 17.6) matching HBM 1000 CE "Ghana" (-11.9 to -4.8, 14.3 to 17.6) and the Koumbi Saleh capital area. Within the canonical Wagadu zone north of the Niger bend. Kept; borderYear set to 1000.

ghana-empire.rationale: Duplicate of africa-ghana-empire (identical polygon). Both cover the Wagadu-Ghana Sahel core c. 1000 CE. Verified against HBM "Ghana" 800-1200.

africa-mali-empire.rationale: Current 52-vertex polygon (-17.4 to 5.3 lon, 10.1 to 18.8 lat) is verbatim HBM "Mali" 1300/1400 — Atlantic coast (Senegambia) east to the middle Niger bend (Gao/Timbuktu) under Mansa Musa. Matches canonical Mansa Musa-era extent.

africa-mali-empire-peak.rationale: Identical 52-vertex polygon to africa-mali-empire. Represents Mansa Musa-era 1325 maximum (Senegambia to middle Niger bend) per HBM "Mali" 1300/1400. Already accurate.

africa-songhai-empire.rationale: Current 24-vertex polygon (-9.4 to 3.6 lon, 11.6 to 19.4 lat) is verbatim HBM "Songhai" 1500 — the Niger bend (Gao, Timbuktu, Djenne) plus much of modern Niger / NE Mali / N Burkina Faso. Sonni Ali / Askia Mohammed-era extent.

africa-kanem-empire.rationale: Current 15-vertex polygon (11.0 to 20.5 lon, 11.0 to 21.0 lat) approximates Kanem at its 13th-century maximum (Dunama Dabbalemi era) — Lake Chad core extending north into Tibesti / Kawar. Wider than HBM "Kanem" 1200 (12.6-19.4 lon, 13.1-16.2 lat) which depicts the Sahelian core only; current extension into Fezzan/Tibesti is plausible per Wikipedia Kanem Empire entry but speculative — marking dashed.

africa-kanem-bornu-empire.rationale: Current 31-vertex polygon (8.34 to 15.82 lon, 3.07 to 21.01 lat) is verbatim HBM "Bornu-Kanem" 1279/1300/1500 — the long N-S Bornu corridor centered on Lake Chad. Note southern tip extends into modern Cameroon (Adamawa) per HBM source; this is acceptable as HBM-canonical.

africa-sokoto-caliphate.rationale: Current 34-vertex polygon (1.46 to 13.20 lon, 7.24 to 18.73 lat) is verbatim HBM "Sokoto Caliphate" 1880 — most of northern Nigeria, southern Niger, northern Cameroon. Matches the canonical Uthman dan Fodio / Caliph Abu Bakr Atiku-era extent.

africa-mossi-wagadougou.rationale: Current 66-vertex polygon (-3.99 to -0.01 lon, 9.39 to 14.74 lat) extends ~1.5deg further north into Sahel than the canonical Mossi heartland on the Volta plateau. Replaced with HBM "Mossi States" 1500 (-3.83 to 0.08 lon, 10.85 to 13.80 lat) which corresponds to the Mossi Naaba kingdoms (Wagadougou, Yatenga, Tenkodogo) in modern Burkina Faso. Reduces oversized northern extent.

africa-hausa-kingdoms.rationale: Current 13-vertex polygon (3.56 to 10.73 lon, 10.91 to 14.52 lat) approximates the seven Hausa Bakwai states (Kano, Katsina, Zaria/Zazzau, Gobir, Rano, Daura, Biram) of northern Nigeria. Compares well with HBM "Hausa States" 1700 (4.82 to 11.08 lon, 9.04 to 16.04 lat); current slightly more compact but within canonical extent.

africa-wassoulou-empire.rationale: Current 93-vertex polygon (-10.0 to -6.0 lon, 7.3 to 13.0 lat) is too narrow east-west: it covers only northern Sierra Leone and southern Guinea but omits the Wassoulou heartland east to Sikasso/Bougouni in southern Mali and N Cote d'Ivoire, which were Samori Toure's core territories before the 1886 treaty with France. Replaced with a hand-crafted peak-extent polygon (-12.5 to -5.0 lon, 7.5 to 12.5 lat) covering Guinea, S Mali to Sikasso, N Sierra Leone, N Liberia, and N Cote d'Ivoire per Wikipedia and africanhistoryextra.com sources.

africa-ife-kingdom.rationale: Current 35-vertex polygon (2.67 to 4.00 lon, 6.37 to 8.99 lat) is shifted slightly west of Ile-Ife (which is at ~4.5E, 7.5N) — the centroid sits over Lagos / E Benin Republic rather than the Ife heartland. Replaced with a corrected polygon (3.0 to 6.0 lon, 6.4 to 9.0 lat) covering Ile-Ife and the 14th-century Yoruba sphere (Owu, Jebba, Tada, Oyo, Ijebu) per Wikipedia "Ife Empire". Marked dashed because Ife was a cultural-religious hegemony more than a centralized state.

africa-benin-kingdom.rationale: Current 68-vertex polygon (4.28 to 6.79 lon, 4.64 to 7.25 lat) matches HBM "Benin" 1500 (3.95 to 7.37 lon, 4.33 to 8.72 lat) for the Benin Empire of the Edo — south-central Nigeria from Lagos border east to Niger Delta. Acceptable as 16c peak.

kingdom-of-benin.rationale: Current 11-vertex polygon (5.4 to 6.5 lon, 5.8 to 6.7 lat) is dramatically undersized — only ~75km square around Benin City — whereas the Benin Empire at its 16th-century peak under Oba Ewuare extended from the Lagos lagoon east to the Niger River and north to ~8N. Replaced with HBM "Benin" 1500.

africa-oyo-empire.rationale: Current 43-vertex polygon (0.51 to 5.68 lon, 6.39 to 9.57 lat) covers the Oyo Yoruba interior of SW Nigeria and SE Benin Republic, matching HBM "Oyo" 1700 (2.42 to 5.34 lon, 6.34 to 10.27 lat) and extending west slightly into Dahomey/Tado tributary zone per peak-era extent under Alaafin Abiodun. Acceptable.

africa-dahomey-kingdom.rationale: Current 44-vertex polygon (1.41 to 2.79 lon, 6.26 to 10.09 lat) is a tall narrow Atlantic-to-Sahel strip, covering Abomey, Allada, and the Dahomey corridor to Atakora — modern Benin Republic. Compares with HBM "Dahomey" 1800 (-0.50 to 4.21 lon, 5.57 to 8.20 lat); current strip is taller/narrower but located correctly. Acceptable as Ghezo/Glele-era peak.

africa-asante-empire.rationale: Current 33-vertex polygon (-3.21 to 0.11 lon, 5.30 to 8.57 lat) is undersized vs the Asante peak under Osei Tutu/Opoku Ware — does not extend west enough into modern Ivory Coast/Comoe region nor north to Salaga and the Volta tributaries. Replaced with HBM "Asante" 1800 (-4.37 to -0.61 lon, 4.70 to 9.16 lat) covering Greater Asante interior of modern Ghana + edge of Cote d'Ivoire.

ashanti-empire.rationale: Current 25-vertex polygon (-4.37 to -0.61 lon, 4.70 to 9.16 lat) is verbatim HBM "Asante" 1800 — already accurate.

africa-igala-kingdom.rationale: Current 10-vertex polygon (6.5 to 8.5 lon, 6.8 to 9.0 lat) is the ~14,000km^2 triangular Igala kingdom at the Niger-Benue confluence (capital Idah on Niger River at ~6.7E, 7.1N). Matches Wikipedia "Igala Kingdom" description. Marked dashed because Igala's influence over Nsukka Igbo / vassal areas south and west was tribute-based and fluctuated.

kingdom-of-axum.rationale: Current 26-vertex polygon (37.80 to 42.41 lon, 13.05 to 15.50 lat) is verbatim HBM "Axum" 400/600 — Tigray/Eritrea highlands. Note: at Ezana-era peak (c.350) Aksum briefly controlled parts of Yemen (Himyar) across the Red Sea; this is not represented but the African-side extent is canonical.

africa-aksumite-empire.rationale: Identical polygon to kingdom-of-axum. Verbatim HBM "Axum" 400/600 (Tigray-Eritrea highlands). Yemen tributary across the Red Sea omitted but African core is canonical.

africa-nobatia-kingdom.rationale: Current 13-vertex polygon (30.7 to 34.0 lon, 19.5 to 24.1 lat) covers Lower Nubia from first to third cataracts. Compares well with HBM "Nobatia" 700 (29.85 to 34.42 lon, 20.12 to 24.02 lat). Acceptable as canonical 6-7c Christian Nubian kingdom.

africa-makuria-kingdom.rationale: Current 12-vertex polygon (28.5 to 36.2 lon, 15.5 to 22.5 lat) covers Upper Nubia from third to fifth cataracts after the merger with Nobatia c.700. Matches canonical Makuria extent (Old Dongola capital ~30E,18N). Marking dashed as borders varied per Wikipedia/Britannica.

africa-nubia-post-meroitic.rationale: Current 17-vertex polygon (29.85 to 34.42 lon, 20.12 to 24.02 lat) — identical bbox to Nobatia — covers Lower Nubia in the post-Meroitic transition period (350-650 CE) before/during the formation of Nobatia. Acceptable as transitional cultural zone (X-Group/Ballana culture).

africa-alodia-kingdom.rationale: Current 14-vertex polygon (33.35 to 34.47 lon, 9.45 to 10.98 lat) is far too small and ~5 degrees too far south — it covers only a strip of upper Blue Nile near the Ethiopian border, not the actual kingdom. Alodia/Alwa was a Christian Nubian kingdom centered at Soba (~15.5N, 32.5E) at the White-Blue Nile confluence, controlling middle Nile from the 6th cataract south to Sennar. Replaced with hand-crafted polygon (31 to 35.5 lon, 11 to 16.5 lat) per Wikipedia/Britannica.

africa-zagwe-dynasty.rationale: Current 39-vertex polygon (35.02 to 40.65 lon, 8.18 to 14.62 lat) extends ~2 degrees too far south into central Ethiopia (Shewan and southern Oromia regions) which the Zagwe never controlled. Per Wikipedia/Britannica, Zagwe ruled "highlands of modern Eritrea and the whole of Tigrai, extending southwards to Waag, Lasta and Damot (Wallo) and thence westwards towards Lake Tana." Replaced with corrected polygon (35.5 to 40.5 lon, 10.5 to 15.5 lat).

africa-solomonic-dynasty.rationale: Current 13-vertex polygon (35.51 to 40.81 lon, 7.11 to 14.52 lat) represents only the medieval Christian highland core. But "Solomonic Dynasty 1270-1974" spans the entire dynasty through Menelik II (Adwa 1896) and Haile Selassie — by 1914 the empire had absorbed Oromia, Harar, Sidamo, Ogaden and most of modern Ethiopia. Replaced with HBM "Abyssinia" 1914 to reflect the full-dynasty peak extent.

ethiopian-empire.rationale: Current 23-vertex polygon (35.46 to 42.46 lon, 6.49 to 15.63 lat) — verbatim HBM "Ethiopia" 1500 — represents only the medieval Christian highland core. The Ethiopian Empire 1270-1974 spans through Menelik II expansion (1880s-1900s) which roughly doubled the territory. Replaced with HBM "Abyssinia" 1914 (33.03 to 47.90 lon, 3.35 to 14.80 lat) to reflect the full-polity peak extent.

africa-ethiopian-empire-medieval.rationale: Current 60-vertex polygon (34.10 to 42.22 lon, 6.64 to 15.14 lat) approximates the medieval Solomonic Christian highland empire (1270-1543) before the Adal jihad and Gragn invasion. Compares well with HBM "Ethiopia" 1500 (35.46 to 42.46 lon, 6.49 to 15.63 lat). Acceptable.

africa-gondar-period.rationale: Current 49-vertex polygon (36.01 to 39.99 lon, 7.02 to 14.88 lat) covers the Solomonic restoration centered at Gondar (37.5E, 12.6N), after the Oromo migrations had reduced the southern Christian frontier.
