Reasonable as Fasilides-Iyasu II peak extent. Marked dashed because southern boundaries were unstable along the Oromo frontier.

africa-ifat-sultanate.rationale: Current 32-vertex polygon (42.01 to 45.37 lon, 8.01 to 11.09 lat) is shifted ~2deg too far east — entirely in modern Somaliland — but Ifat's heartland was in eastern Shewa (Yifat district at ~39.5E, 10N) of modern Ethiopia, extending east through the Awash valley to Zeila on the Gulf of Aden. Replaced with corrected polygon (39 to 43.5 lon, 8.5 to 12 lat) covering the Shewa-to-Zeila corridor per Wikipedia and Britannica.

africa-adal-sultanate.rationale: Current 52-vertex polygon (39.38 to 46.18 lon, 6.73 to 12.10 lat) covers the Adal Sultanate at the peak of Ahmad Gragn (1529-1543) when Adal conquered most of Ethiopian highlands plus the Somali/Djibouti coast. HBM "Adal" 1500 is more conservative (41.5-44.3 lon, 9.5-11.8 lat) representing pre-jihad extent only; current peak-Gragn extent is canonical.

africa-ajuran-sultanate.rationale: Current 15-vertex polygon (40.5 to 51.4 lon, -0.5 to 11.5 lat) extends too far northeast to ~51E,11.5N — into the Majeerteen/Puntland region of NE Somalia which Ajuran did not control. Ajuran's northern limit was around Hobyo (~5.4N) and east never reached Cape Guardafui. Replaced with corrected polygon (41 to 49.5 lon, -0.4 to 8 lat) covering the interriverine Jubba-Shebelle zone and coast from Kismayo north to Hobyo per Wikipedia and Britannica.

africa-funj-sultanate.rationale: Current 55-vertex polygon (28.77 to 36.47 lon, 10.34 to 17.64 lat) covers the Funj/Sennar Sultanate at peak (16-17c) — middle Nile Gezira plus extensions into Kordofan (west) and Berber (north). Wider than HBM "Funj" 1500 (31.78 to 34.58 lon, 10.98 to 16.51 lat) which is the early-Funj core only; current extent is canonical 17c-Funj per Wikipedia.

africa-buganda-kingdom.rationale: Current 29-vertex polygon (30.89 to 33.89 lon, -0.97 to 1.86 lat) covers Buganda on the north-west shore of Lake Victoria — matches HBM "Buganda" 1900 (30.81 to 33.32 lon, -1.53 to 1.53 lat) and 1815 (30.30 to 33.51 lon, -1.28 to 2.19 lat). Mutesa I-era extent.

africa-bunyoro-kitara.rationale: Current 36-vertex polygon (30.19 to 32.89 lon, -0.40 to 2.87 lat) covers Bunyoro-Kitara north of Buganda, west of L. Albert. Matches HBM "Bunyoro" 1900 (29.82 to 33.35 lon, -0.45 to 2.66 lat). Kabarega-era core (which historically claimed larger Kitara empire that included Toro and Ankole).

africa-toro-kingdom.rationale: Current 23-vertex polygon (29.55 to 31.00 lon, -1.47 to 0.96 lat) extends too far south to -1.47S — that's inside Ankole/Rwanda territory. Toro Kingdom (founded 1830 by Kaboyo Olimi I, son of Bunyoro's Kyebambe III) lay between Lake Albert and Lake Edward in W Uganda, with the Muziizi River as its northern boundary with Bunyoro. Replaced with corrected polygon (29.7 to 31.2 lon, 0.0 to 1.4 lat) per Wikipedia "Tooro Kingdom".

africa-ankole-kingdom.rationale: Current 34-vertex polygon (29.55 to 31.70 lon, -1.48 to 0.70 lat) extends too far north to 0.70N which is Toro territory; Ankole (Nkore) lay south of Toro, east of L. Edward, north of Rwanda — centered on Isingiro/Mbarara (~30.7E, -0.6N). Replaced with corrected polygon (29.8 to 31.7 lon, -1.5 to 0.0 lat) per Wikipedia "Ankole".

africa-rwanda-kingdom.rationale: Current 56-vertex polygon (28.86 to 30.89 lon, -2.83 to -1.07 lat) covers Rwanda (Banyarwanda kingdom) — slightly larger than HBM "Rwanda" 1900 (29.48 to 31.19 lon, -2.71 to -1.11 lat) to include pre-colonial westward extent. Acceptable as 19c Mwami Kigeli IV-era peak.

africa-burundi-kingdom.rationale: Current 56-vertex polygon (28.99 to 30.83 lon, -4.46 to -2.30 lat) matches HBM "Burundi" 1900 (29.31 to 30.72 lon, -4.47 to -3.01 lat) and extends north slightly into pre-colonial Mwami-controlled zone. Acceptable.

africa-kongo-kingdom.rationale: Current 69-vertex polygon (11.78 to 17.22 lon, -9.40 to -2.87 lat) covers the Kingdom of Kongo at peak under Afonso I — N Angola, W DRC (Bas-Congo / Kwango), and S Congo-Brazzaville (Loango tributary). HBM "Congo" 1500 (12.37 to 15.05 lon, -9.37 to -4.77 lat) covers only the core; current peak extent is canonical per Wikipedia. Eastern extent to 17E into Kasai is at the limit but plausible for Mbanza-Kongo's sphere.

ndongo-kingdom.rationale: Current 62-vertex polygon (12.45 to 16.99 lon, -11.99 to -6.01 lat) extends too far south to -12S (south of Benguela) which is outside the Mbundu/Ndongo zone (south of the Cuanza was already Bantu Ovimbundu territory). Also extends slightly too far north. Ndongo's core was between the Cuanza and Lucala rivers in the highlands east of Luanda, capital Kabasa, peak under Ngola Kiluanji (late 16c) reaching the Atlantic at Luanda. Replaced with corrected polygon (13.2 to 17.0 lon, -10.5 to -7.5 lat) per Wikipedia/Britannica.

africa-luba-empire.rationale: Current 13-vertex polygon (23.5 to 29.0 lon, -10.5 to -5.0 lat) covers the Luba Empire of the Upper Lualaba (Katanga plateau) under Mwata Kalala Ilunga — matches HBM "Luba" 1700 (23.26 to 31.08 lon, -10.40 to -5.14 lat) closely, current slightly more conservative on the east. Acceptable.

luba-kingdom.rationale: Current 18-vertex polygon (23.0 to 27.8 lon, -9.3 to -7.0 lat) is undersized vs the Luba peak — missing the SE extension into modern Zambian copperbelt and the SW into Kasai. Replaced with HBM "Luba" 1700 (23.26 to 31.08 lon, -10.40 to -5.14 lat) which is the canonical Luba Empire footprint.

africa-lunda-empire.rationale: Current 12-vertex polygon (18.5 to 25.5 lon, -12.0 to -6.5 lat) covers the Lunda Empire of the Mwata Yamvo (Mwaant Yaav) on the Katanga-Kasai plateau — matches HBM "Lunda" 1800 (17.47 to 23.63 lon, -11.12 to -6.71 lat) with eastward extension to include Kazembe tributary. Acceptable as Lunda commonwealth peak.

africa-great-zimbabwe.rationale: Current 30-vertex polygon (27.77 to 31.93 lon, -21.04 to -17.12 lat) covers the Great Zimbabwe state core (capital at ~30.9E, -20.3S) on the Zimbabwe plateau between Zambezi and Limpopo. Compares with HBM "Great Zimbabwe" 1300 (28.28 to 33.40 lon, -23.05 to -18.64 lat); current is more conservative on east (does not include Mozambique tributary zone) but properly covers the plateau core c.1100-1450.

kingdom-of-zimbabwe.rationale: Current 33-vertex polygon (26.54 to 33.04 lon, -22.33 to -16.71 lat) matches HBM "Great Zimbabwe" 1300 (28.28 to 33.40 lon, -23.05 to -18.64 lat). Slightly wider on the west into eastern Botswana (Mapungubwe successor zone). Acceptable.

africa-mutapa-empire.rationale: Current 35-vertex polygon (27.38 to 34.18 lon, -21.32 to -14.88 lat) covers the Mutapa Empire (post-Great Zimbabwe northern successor under Nyatsimba Mutota) — N Zimbabwe + W Mozambique + S Zambia. Compares with HBM "Mwenemutapa" 1500 (28.02 to 33.66 lon, -25.87 to -16.07 lat); current omits HBM's southern Limpopo extension but matches the canonical post-Great Zimbabwe northern Mutapa peak.

africa-monomutapa.rationale: Identical polygon to africa-mutapa-empire (35 vertices, 27.38 to 34.18 lon, -21.32 to -14.88 lat). Same Mutapa/Munhumutapa Empire — Portuguese cartographic name. Already accurate.

africa-mwene-mutapa-empire.rationale: Current 68-vertex polygon (25.22 to 32.98 lon, -22.34 to -14.47 lat) extends ~3 degrees too far west into the Kalahari/eastern Botswana (the Hwange/Makgadikgadi region), which Mwene Mutapa never controlled. Replaced with HBM "Mwenemutapa" 1500 (28.02 to 33.66 lon, -25.87 to -16.07 lat) which is the canonical 15-16c peak (N Zimbabwe + W Mozambique + lower Zambezi).

africa-torwa-state.rationale: Current 54-vertex polygon (22.01 to 27.99 lon, -24.98 to -17.78 lat) covers the Torwa state at Khami (capital ~28.5E, -20.2S, but current bbox is shifted slightly west to include the Mapungubwe successor zone and Butua). Per Wikipedia/zimfieldguide, Torwa's area "included present-day southern and south-western Zimbabwe, north-east Botswana, and northern South Africa" — current bbox reasonable.

africa-rozvi-empire.rationale: Current 36-vertex polygon (26.48 to 32.15 lon, -22.27 to -16.90 lat) covers the Rozvi Empire on the Zimbabwe plateau (Changamire dynasty c. 1684-1830). Per Wikipedia/Britannica, Rozvi influence "extended over much of present-day Zimbabwe and perhaps westward into Botswana and southward into northeastern South Africa." Current bbox matches.

africa-maravi-confederacy.rationale: Current 55-vertex polygon (31.01 to 36.99 lon, -18.98 to -11.02 lat) covers the Maravi Confederacy at peak (17c under Kalonga Masula) — Lake Malawi southern shore, Lower Shire, Zambezi valley, into central/N Mozambique. Per Britannica/Wikipedia "stretched north of the Zambezi River to the Dwangwa River, west to the Luangwa River, and east to the Mozambique coast." Acceptable.

africa-zulu-kingdom.rationale: Current 62-vertex polygon (28.83 to 32.71 lon, -30.63 to -25.90 lat) covers the Zulu Kingdom under Shaka/Dingane — KwaZulu-Natal from Tugela to Pongola, west to Drakensberg. Matches HBM "Zulu" 1815 (28.43 to 32.89 lon, -30.92 to -26.26 lat). Acceptable.

africa-mthethwa-paramountcy.rationale: Current 45-vertex polygon (29.69 to 32.80 lon, -29.57 to -26.21 lat) extends too far south into Pondoland/Mpondo territory and too far west into Drakensberg foothills. Per Wikipedia/Britannica, Mthethwa was "south of the lower Mfolozi River in the northeastern part of present-day KwaZulu-Natal" — a coastal chieftaincy roughly from St Lucia bay south to the Tugela mouth. Replaced with corrected polygon (30.5 to 32.5 lon, -29.0 to -27.0 lat) per Cambridge History/Wikipedia.

africa-swaziland-kingdom.rationale: Current 23-vertex polygon (30.78 to 32.12 lon, -27.32 to -25.74 lat) covers modern Eswatini (formerly Swaziland) plus eastern Transvaal claims. Matches HBM "Swaziland" 1900 (30.56 to 31.73 lon, -27.64 to -25.69 lat). Acceptable for Mswati II / Sobhuza II-era.

africa-lesotho-kingdom.rationale: Current 56-vertex polygon (27.00 to 29.44 lon, -30.66 to -28.57 lat) matches HBM "Lesotho" 1914 (27.07 to 29.44 lon, -30.79 to -28.72 lat) — modern Lesotho borders set by 1869 Treaty of Aliwal North after the Free State-Basotho Wars. Acceptable.

africa-sotho-kingdom.rationale: Current 56-vertex polygon (27.00 to 29.44 lon, -30.66 to -28.57 lat) — identical to africa-lesotho-kingdom — represents the Sotho kingdom under Moshoeshoe I before the 1869 Treaty of Aliwal North. Note: Moshoeshoe's pre-treaty Basotho state initially extended west of the Caledon to ~26E; the current polygon represents post-1869/modern Lesotho borders, slightly conservative but acceptable as the "settled" extent.

africa-ndebele-kingdom.rationale: Current 46-vertex polygon (26.31 to 30.62 lon, -22.19 to -17.92 lat) covers the Matabele/Ndebele Kingdom of Mzilikazi/Lobengula in SW Zimbabwe + edge of Botswana, capital at Bulawayo (~28.6E, -20.2S). Wider than HBM "Ndebele" 1900 (25.60 to 29.20 lon, -20.60 to -18.39 lat) — current includes the northern/eastern Ndebele expansion zone to ~22S. Acceptable.

africa-south-african-republic.rationale: Current 58-vertex polygon (25.05 to 31.18 lon, -27.77 to -22.56 lat) matches HBM "Transvaal" 1900 (25.05 to 31.94 lon, -27.54 to -21.53 lat). South African Republic (ZAR) at peak before the 2nd Anglo-Boer War. Acceptable.

africa-orange-free-state.rationale: Current 80-vertex polygon (23.98 to 29.65 lon, -31.77 to -26.40 lat) matches HBM "Orange Free State" 1900 (24.17 to 29.38 lon, -30.55 to -26.50 lat) with slight southern extension. Acceptable as Boer republic pre-1902.

africa-imerina-madagascar.rationale: Current 138-vertex polygon (43.93 to 49.95 lon, -23.73 to -14.32 lat) covers essentially the entire island of Madagascar — appropriate for the post-1817 Imerina Kingdom of Madagascar (recognized as Kingdom of Madagascar under Radama I) which by Ranavalona I/Radama II era controlled most of the island. Matches HBM "Imerina" 1900 (45.66 to 50.50 lon, -23.55 to -14.12 lat) plus western highlands.

merina-kingdom.rationale: Current 10-vertex polygon (45.29 to 48.49 lon, -23.59 to -16.90 lat) is verbatim HBM "Expansionist Kingdom of Merina" 1000-1815 — the Imerina central highlands core (Antananarivo at 47.5E, -18.9S). Pre-Radama I central core; coexists with africa-imerina-madagascar (which is the full-island peak).

africa-omani-zanzibar.rationale: Current 200-vertex polygon (37.36 to 40.31 lon, -10.37 to -1.86 lat) is a narrow coastal strip from Pemba south to Cabo Delgado, but Omani Zanzibar at peak (Sayyid Said, c.1830-1856) claimed coastal authority from Mogadishu (~1.2N) south to Cabo Delgado (~-11.2S), plus inland caravan routes. Replaced with HBM "Sultinate of Zanzibar" 1900 (36.04 to 43.33 lon, -11.21 to 1.20 lat) which includes the north Somali claims and Pemba/Mafia.

africa-zanzibar-sultanate.rationale: Identical narrow-strip polygon to africa-omani-zanzibar. The Sultanate of Zanzibar (1856-1964, post-split from Oman) claimed coastal authority including the Somali coast (Brava, Merca, Mogadishu) until 1888, plus inland caravan stations. Replaced with HBM "Sultinate of Zanzibar" 1900 (36.04 to 43.33 lon, -11.21 to 1.20 lat).

khedivate-of-egypt.rationale: Current 109-vertex polygon (21.81 to 38.60 lon, 3.49 to 31.66 lat) covers the Khedivate of Egypt at peak (Ismail Pasha, c.1879) — Egypt proper + Anglo-Egyptian Sudan + Equatoria + Suakin/Red Sea coast + Eritrea coast. Per Wikipedia "Khedivate of Egypt." Western extent to 21.8E excludes most of Darfur (annexed 1874-1882) but otherwise comprehensive. Acceptable for African-territories peak.

asia-ferghana.rationale: OUT-OF-SCOPE for the Africa subset: Kingdom of Ferghana (Davan) is a Central Asian polity in the Ferghana Valley (modern Uzbekistan/Kyrgyzstan/Tajikistan), not African. This entry was mis-grouped in africa.json subset. Current polygon (69.01 to 74.99 lon, 38.80 to 41.70 lat) is reasonable for the Ferghana Valley — defer to central_asia_steppe audit.

americas-portuguese-brazil-1700.rationale: Current geometry (bbox [-50.18,-28.56,-34.89,-1.60], 149 vertices, rel-area 62.44) is the verbatim HBM-1700 'Portuguese Brazil' polygon, which is anomalously narrow -- only the SE coastal strip from southern Rio Grande do Sul to Espirito Santo. By 1700 Portuguese effective control included the NE captaincies (Pernambuco recovered from the Dutch in 1654; Bahia was the colonial capital; Rio Grande do Norte, Paraiba, Ceara were established; Maranhao/Para constituted the separate Estado do Maranhao founded 1621 with Sao Luis and Belem). Test points Recife (-34.88,-8.07), Salvador (-38.51,-12.97), Belem (-48.50,-1.46), Sao Luis (-44.31,-2.53) all fall OUTSIDE the current polygon. Replaced with the HBM-1715 'Vice-Royalty of Brazil' polygon which extends NE to Maranhao and inland to the Sao Francisco cattle frontier and is the closest accurate canonical source for c. 1700 Portuguese Brazil.

americas-viceroyalty-new-spain-1600.rationale: Current geometry (bbox [-118.36,8.03,-65.27,32.71], 1124 vertices) covers Mexico, Central America to the Panama border, the Greater Antilles (Cuba/Hispaniola/Puerto Rico), and a band of northern Mexico to ~32.7N. This is consistent with the de jure Viceroyalty of New Spain c. 1600: the Audiencias of Mexico, Nueva Galicia, Guadalajara, Guatemala, plus the Caribbean (Audiencia of Santo Domingo, which was a New Spain audiencia). Panama is correctly excluded -- in 1600 it was under the Audiencia of Panama within the Viceroyalty of Peru. The far-northern extent to ~32.7N is a paper claim (only Santa Fe NM, founded 1610, and Florida had settlement) but is defensible. Two-way overlap with HBM-1600 New Spain is 75% (source in current), 39% (current in source) -- the discrepancy is mainly the Caribbean (correctly in the current) and the northern claim band (HBM omits it). MINOR GAP: Venezuela (Caracas, Maracaibo, Cumana, Margarita) was governed by the Audiencia of Santo Domingo and thus nominally part of New Spain until 1786. HBM-1600 extends east to -61.41 lon to include Venezuela; current stops at -65.27. Keeping the current geometry as 'accurate' since the Venezuela inclusion is at the edge of the de-jure vs de-facto debate and most modern atlases assign Venezuela to a separate captaincy. If the dataset wants strict de-jure 1600 New Spain, extend the eastern boundary to Cape Codera (~ -66 lon) and south to ~ 8 lat.

americas-viceroyalty-peru-1600.rationale: Current geometry (bbox [-109.44,-55.92,-57.47,1.43], 2324 vertices, rel-area 294.96) covers only the Pacific axis: Ecuador, Peru, Bolivia, Chile, and southern Patagonia. This is fundamentally wrong for c. 1600: the Viceroyalty of Peru at that date was ALL Spanish South America except the Venezuelan coast (which was under Audiencia de Santo Domingo). Test points missing from the current polygon: Bogota (-74.07,4.71), Panama City (-79.5,9.0), Buenos Aires (-58.4,-34.6), Cordoba (-64.18,-31.41), Asuncion (-57.58,-25.26). Per the Wikipedia / Britannica record, Peru did not cede New Granada (Colombia/Ecuador/Panama/Venezuela) until 1717/1739, and did not cede the Rio de la Plata basin (Argentina/Uruguay/Paraguay/Bolivia) until 1776. The HBM-1700 'Vice Royalty of Peru' polygon (bbox -82.98,-41.79, -52.05,12.43, rel-area 328.72) is essentially identical to what 1600 Peru should look like and is the recommended replacement -- it includes Panama, Colombia, the Argentine pampas, Cuyo, Paraguay, and the entire Andean axis to ~ -42 lat. Replaced.

americas-british-thirteen-colonies.rationale: Current geometry (bbox [-84.29,32.47,-69.93,45.02], 726 vertices) has three inaccuracies for the 1607-1776 Thirteen Colonies: (a) Western extent reaches ~ -84 lon (into modern KY/TN/OH), well past the Appalachian crest. After the Royal Proclamation of 1763 these lands were Indian Reserve and after the 1774 Quebec Act they were assigned to Quebec; they were never part of any of the 13 colonies' organized territory. Spurious: Pittsburgh (-79.99,40.44), Cumberland MD (-78.76,39.65), Buffalo (-78.88,42.89), the entire lon -82 to -84 band. (b) Georgia coast is mostly cut off -- Savannah (-81.10,32.08) falls outside the polygon despite Georgia being the 13th colony chartered 1732. The polygon's southern boundary should reach the St Marys River (~ 30.7 lat) per the 1763 settlement. (c) Maine is mostly excluded -- Portland ME (-70.26,43.66), Augusta ME (-69.78,44.31) are outside the polygon, despite Maine being administered by Massachusetts colony from 1652 until statehood 1820. Recommended correction: retract the western boundary to the Appalachian crest (approx: NY -75, PA -77 to -79 along the watershed, VA/MD -79.5, NC -81.5, SC -82, GA -83 in the upper Piedmont); extend southern boundary down the Atlantic to the St Marys River (~30.7 lat); extend northern boundary up Maine to ~46-47N (Penobscot/St Croix). Marking as dashed (uncertain) given the multiple geometry issues; no clean single-source HBM polygon exists for this empire (HBM-1715 'British American colonies' is too narrow on the southern end).

americas-new-france-1700.rationale: Current geometry (bbox [-96.03,38.34,-64.69,55.25], 531 vertices) shows three inaccuracies for the 1608-1763 New France: (a) ACADIA IS MISSING. Halifax (-63.58,44.65), Cape Breton (-60.20,46.13), Charlottetown PEI (-63.13,46.24), New Brunswick (-66.07,45.27) -- all outside the polygon. Acadia was core New France from 1604 (Port-Royal) until ceded to Britain at Utrecht 1713; Cape Breton (Ile-Royale) and PEI (Ile-Saint-Jean) remained French until 1758. For a 1700 borderYear the entire Acadia must be included. (b) LOUISIANA IS MISSING. La Salle claimed the Mississippi for France in 1682; Iberville founded Louisiana at Biloxi 1699 and Fort Louis (Mobile) 1702. The 1700 claim ran down the Mississippi to the Gulf. Currently New Orleans (-90.07,29.95), Mobile (-88.04,30.69), Biloxi (-88.89,30.39) all outside. (c) BOSTON SPURIOUSLY INCLUDED. Boston (-71.06,42.36) is INSIDE the current polygon, but Boston was a Massachusetts Bay Colony (English) settlement from 1630. Pull the southeastern boundary back to roughly the Kennebec or Penobscot watershed in present-day Maine (~ -70 lon). Note also that HBM-1700 'New France' is anomalously small (St Lawrence valley only, rel-area 6.36) and should not be used as a corrective source. Recommended correction is editorial: add Acadia (NS/NB/PEI/Cape Breton); add a Mississippi-corridor + lower Louisiana lobe down to the Gulf at ~ 29 lat between -89 and -91 lon; clip the eastern boundary out of MA. Marking dashed.

americas-viceroyalty-new-granada.rationale: Current geometry (bbox [-91.67,-4.99,-59.82,12.47], 741 vertices, rel-area 194.07) correctly covers all four constituent territories of the Viceroyalty of New Granada 1717-1819: Panama (Panama City -79.5,9.0), Colombia (Bogota -74.07,4.71; Cali -76.53,3.45), Ecuador (Quito -78.46,-0.18), and Venezuela (Caracas -66.91,10.5; Maracaibo -71.62,10.66). Two-way overlap with HBM-1783 New Granada is 98% (current in source) / 75% (source in current). Minor: HBM-1783 extends east to ~ -48 lon to cover the Captaincy General of Venezuela's Guayana province along the Orinoco; current stops at -59.82 lon. This is a minor underextension but within tolerance for a 'settled' representation. Kept as accurate.

americas-portuguese-brazil-1750.rationale: Current geometry (bbox [-74.02,-33.74,-34.79,5.27], 1026 vertices, rel-area 707.02) closely matches HBM-1783 'Vice-Royalty of Brazil' (bbox -73.89,-33.88,-34.89,5.69, rel-area 674.44) at 94% (current in source) / 98% (source in current). This represents the post-Treaty of Madrid (1750) territorial settlement that replaced the Tordesillas line with uti possidetis and established Brazil's borders close to their modern form: the Amazon basin (Manaus included), Mato Grosso (Cuiaba included), the NE interior, and the entire Atlantic coast from Maranhao (Sao Luis) south to Rio Grande do Sul. Test points Salvador, Belo Horizonte, SP, Curitiba, Porto Alegre, Brasilia, Cuiaba, Fortaleza, Natal, Manaus all correctly inside. A few individual coastal cities (Recife -34.88,-8.07; Rio -43.17,-22.91; Belem -48.50,-1.46; Sao Luis -44.31,-2.53) fall on the polygon edge but the surrounding regions are correctly included -- this is a rasterization artifact, not a territorial error. Kept.

americas-british-north-america-canada.rationale: Current geometry (bbox [-141.00,41.67,-52.62,83.12], 7546 vertices, rel-area 1686.27) covers the full Canadian outline including all federation provinces, Rupert's Land (Hudson Bay watershed), Newfoundland (incl. Labrador), the western Yukon to the 141W meridian (the 1825 Russian-British boundary), and the Arctic Archipelago to 83N. For a 1763-1867 BNA envelope this is correct: it includes (i) the Province of Quebec (post-1791 Upper + Lower Canada / post-1841 Province of Canada / post-1867 Quebec + Ontario); (ii) Newfoundland (separate colony); (iii) Nova Scotia + New Brunswick + PEI + Cape Breton (Maritimes); (iv) Hudson's Bay Company territory (Rupert's Land + North-Western Territory transferred to Canada 1870); (v) correctly EXCLUDES British Columbia (Vancouver -123.12,49.28 outside the polygon) which joined the federation in 1871. Test points Saguenay (-71.07,48.42), Toronto (-79.38,43.65), Fredericton (-66.66,45.96), Sydney NS (-60.20,46.13), Truro NS (-63.27,45.36), Winnipeg (-97.14,49.9), Calgary (-114.07,51.04), Yellowknife (-114.37,62.45), Whitehorse (-135.05,60.72), St John's NL (-52.71,47.56) all correctly inside. A few coastal city points (Quebec City -71.21,46.81; Halifax -63.58,44.65; Charlottetown -63.13,46.24) appear outside but this is a coastal-vertex precision artifact -- inland points in the same regions are inside. Kept.

americas-viceroyalty-rio-de-la-plata.rationale: Current geometry (bbox [-73.59,-55.05,-53.11,-9.68], 565 vertices, rel-area 423.22) correctly covers all four constituent territories of the Viceroyalty of the Rio de la Plata 1776-1814: Argentina (incl. pampas and Cuyo and Patagonia), Uruguay (Banda Oriental), Paraguay, and Bolivia (Audiencia de Charcas / Upper Peru). Per the 1776 founding decree, the Viceroyalty explicitly included the Real Audiencia of Charcas (Potosi, La Paz, Santa Cruz) and the Intendancy of Paraguay -- both of which are missing from the HBM-1783 polygon but PRESENT in the current geometry, making the current MORE accurate than HBM here. Two-way overlap with HBM-1783 is 51% (current in source) / 98% (source in current) -- the current is a proper superset of HBM. Wikipedia / Britannica unambiguously confirm Bolivia and Paraguay as Rio de la Plata territory until the wars of independence. Far southern Patagonia (south of ~ -42 lat) is a nominal claim but standard de-jure mapping convention. Kept as accurate.

americas-united-states-1790.rationale: Current geometry (bbox [-89.31,31.05,-69.10,45.88], 798 vertices, rel-area 154.42) correctly represents the United States in 1790 (post-Treaty of Paris 1783, pre-Louisiana Purchase 1803): the 13 original states plus the Northwest Territory and Southwest Territory between the Appalachians and the Mississippi. Western boundary at ~ -89.3 lon = the Mississippi River; southern boundary at lat 31.05 = the 31st parallel which was the 1783 / Pinckney's Treaty 1795 boundary with Spanish West Florida; eastern boundary the Atlantic coast; northern boundary the British line. Test points Boston (-71.06,42.36), NYC (-74.0,40.7), Detroit (-83.05,42.33), Atlanta (-84.39,33.75), Nashville (-86.78,36.16), Pittsburgh (-79.99,40.44), Cleveland (-81.69,41.49) all correctly inside; Houston, New Orleans, Pensacola, Mobile, Memphis, St Louis, Miami all correctly OUTSIDE (Spanish territory in 1790). Note that HBM-1783 USA is over-drawn (extends west to -95 and south to 25N) and should NOT be used as a corrective reference -- the current geometry is more accurate than the HBM. Kept.

americas-russian-america-alaska.rationale: Current geometry (bbox [-178.87,51.36,179.77,71.35], 868 vertices, 79 polygons including Aleutian islands) covers Alaska mainland plus the Aleutian and Pribilof and St Lawrence and Kodiak Islands -- matching HBM-1815 'Russian Empire' (Alaska portion) at 91-93% two-way overlap. However it OMITS Fort Ross / Krepost Ross, the Russian-American Company's outpost in Sonoma County, California (1812-1841) at -123.24, 38.51 -- which was the southernmost Russian possession in the Americas and an iconic part of the 1799-1867 Russian America empire. Replaced with the HBM-1815 Russian Empire polygon UNION a small Fort Ross polygon (bbox approx -123.4 to -123.18 lon, 38.4 to 38.58 lat). The Alaska interior is included (de jure RAC charter to the watersheds); effective control was coastal + along the Yukon / Kuskokwim / Nushagak / Stikine river basins, but the de-jure boundary to the 141W meridian + Bering Strait is the standard representation.

americas-united-states-1804.rationale: Current geometry (bbox [-114.04,26.45,-69.71,48.92], 684 vertices, rel-area 562.25) intends to depict the US after the Louisiana Purchase (Dec 1803 / formal handover Mar 1804). The eastern and northern boundaries are correct (Atlantic coast; 49th parallel west of Lake of the Woods although that line was not formally established until 1818). However three discrete spurious inclusions: (a) SPANISH TEXAS: Houston (-95.37,29.76) and the Gulf coast east-of-Sabine band are inside the polygon. Texas was Tejas under New Spain in 1804; the Sabine River (~ -94 lon) boundary was settled by the Adams-Onis Treaty of 1819. (b) SPANISH WEST FLORIDA: Pensacola (-87.21,30.42) is inside. West Florida was Spanish until annexed in stages 1810 (Baton Rouge area), 1813 (Mobile), 1819 (Pensacola). For 1804 the entire Gulf coast from the Mississippi delta east to St Marys River was Spanish. (c) SOUTHERN ARIZONA: Phoenix (-112.07,33.45) is inside. The Pimeria Alta region was Spanish New Spain; transferred to the US only by the 1848 Mexican Cession + 1853 Gadsden Purchase. Recommended correction: clip out Spanish Texas (south of ~ 32 lat west of the Sabine River), the Pensacola/Mobile coastal strip (West Florida), and the southern Arizona lobe (south of ~ 35 lat west of -109 lon). Western boundary should run roughly along the Continental Divide (~ -106 to -109 lon depending on latitude). Marking dashed given the multiple spurious areas; HBM-1800 USA is too restrictive (does not include the Louisiana Purchase) and not a clean corrective source.

americas-olmec-heartland.rationale: Current geometry bbox [-95.79, 16.51, -92.21, 18.72] extends too far south into the Oaxaca highlands. The Olmec heartland is the southern Gulf Coast lowlands of Veracruz (San Lorenzo Tenochtitlán, Tres Zapotes) and Tabasco (La Venta) — roughly 17-19N, -96 to -92W. Replace with HBM 'Olmec' (-500) polygon which captures the canonical heartland.
sources: Diehl, R. (2004). The Olmecs: America's First Civilization. Thames & Hudson.

americas-zapotec-monte-alban.rationale: Current bbox [-97.99, 15.66, -95.01, 18.49] is reasonable but over-extends slightly. Replace with HBM 'Monte Albán' polygon (-100 CE, peak Period II) which is tightly fitted to the Valley of Oaxaca and adjacent Ejutla/Miahuatlán/Tlacolula sub-valleys.
sources: Blanton, R. (1978). Monte Alban: Settlement Patterns at the Ancient Zapotec Capital.

americas-hopewell-culture.rationale: Current geometry already sourced from HBM Hopewell Culture (100 CE). Bbox [-95.79, 35.79, -75.59, 45.76] correctly represents the Hopewell Interaction Sphere — Ohio Valley core with exchange network spanning the Eastern Woodlands.

americas-adena-culture.rationale: Current bbox [-86.0, 37.6, -79.9, 40.9] matches Adena heartland in the middle Ohio Valley (modern Ohio, Kentucky, West Virginia, Indiana). HBM Adena Culture bbox [-85.97, 36.96, -78.32, 41.45] is similar.
sources: Webb, W. & Snow, C. (1945). The Adena People.

americas-hohokam.rationale: Bbox [-113.5, 31.6, -110.1, 34.05] correctly covers the Sonoran Desert Hohokam range — Salt and Gila river basins of southern Arizona with adjacent northern Sonora. Northern cap at 34N appropriately excludes the Mogollon Rim country.
sources: Bayman, J. (2001). The Hohokam of southwest North America.

americas-ancestral-pueblo.rationale: Current bbox [-123.65, 22.87, -102.57, 38.88] grossly overreaches into California, Baja California, and central Mexico — the source HBM polygon appears to be the result of a polygon-grouping bug. Ancestral Puebloan (Anasazi) is the Four Corners region: SE Utah, SW Colorado, NE Arizona, NW New Mexico (roughly 34.5-38.5N, -111.5 to -106.5W). Replace with bounding polygon for the canonical Anasazi range.
sources: Plog, S. (1997). Ancient Peoples of the American Southwest. Thames & Hudson.
Cordell, L. & McBrinn, M. (2012). Archaeology of the Southwest, 3rd ed.

americas-teotihuacan.rationale: Current bbox [-99.7, 18.7, -97.7, 20.4] covers only the Valley of Mexico. Teotihuacan's directly-administered domain extended west into Hidalgo and parts of Estado de México, north to Tula corridor, east into Puebla and Tlaxcala. Replace with HBM 'Teotihuacán' polygon (100 CE) bbox [-101.01, 18.92, -98.48, 20.90].
sources: Cowgill, G. (1997). State and Society at Teotihuacan, Mexico. Annual Review of Anthropology 26.

americas-mogollon-culture.rationale: Current bbox [-110.5, 29.5, -105.5, 34.5] covers the Mogollon heartland: SE Arizona, SW New Mexico, far West Texas, and northern Sonora/Chihuahua. HBM 'Mogollon' (800) polygon extends much further south (to ~20N) which conflates Mogollon with Mesoamerican periphery — current geometry is preferable.
sources: Cordell, L. & McBrinn, M. (2012). Archaeology of the Southwest, 3rd ed.
Reid, J. & Whittlesey, S. (1997). The Archaeology of Ancient Arizona.

americas-maya-classic.rationale: Bbox [-92.95, 13.51, -86.01, 22.58] captures the Classic Maya lowlands and highlands: Yucatán peninsula (Mexico), Petén (Guatemala), Belize, parts of Chiapas, western Honduras, western El Salvador. Acceptable as a Maya cultural area polygon. HBM 'Maya city-states' (800) covers essentially the same region.
sources: Sharer, R. & Traxler, L. (2006). The Ancient Maya, 6th ed.

maya-classic-period.rationale: Identical geometry to americas-maya-classic (bbox and vertex count match). Same audit conclusion applies. Recommend deduplicating in source data.

americas-ancestral-fremont.rationale: Bbox [-114.0, 36.5, -108.5, 42.0] covers Fremont culture range: most of Utah, eastern Nevada, western Colorado, southwestern Wyoming, southern Idaho. Reasonable cultural-extent polygon; could be extended slightly north to capture extreme northern Fremont sites in S. Wyoming/S. Idaho.
sources: Madsen, D. & Simms, S. (1998). The Fremont Complex. Journal of World Prehistory 12.

americas-tiwanaku.rationale: Current geometry is the HBM 'Tiahuanaco Empire' polygon (bbox [-71.61, -25.55, -67.24, -14.11]). Covers Lake Titicaca basin, Bolivian altiplano, southern Peru coast, north Chile. The southern extent (-25.5) reflects Tiwanaku colonial/influence sites in northern Chile (Cochabamba/San Pedro de Atacama); this is contested but acceptable.

tiahuanaco-empire.rationale: Duplicate of americas-tiwanaku with slightly less accurate geometry (bbox [-71.78, -19.30, -66.19, -12.78] truncates Tiwanaku's southern reach into northern Chile/N. Argentina). Replace with the same HBM Tiahuanaco Empire polygon used for americas-tiwanaku.

americas-calusa-chiefdom.rationale: Bbox [-82.74, 24.55, -80.03, 28.49] covers South Florida coast (Tampa Bay south to Florida Keys, including the Caloosahatchee-Estero region, Lake Okeechobee, and Florida Keys). Matches Calusa range. HBM 'Calusa' (1492) polygon similar.
sources: Marquardt, W. (1988). Politics and Production among the Calusa.

americas-wari-huari.rationale: Current geometry is the HBM 'Huari Empire' polygon (bbox [-78.51, -17.22, -69.87, -7.02]). Covers central Peruvian highlands (Ayacucho core) and extends through the Andes — canonical Wari Empire extent.
sources: Isbell, W. & McEwan, G. (1991). Huari Administrative Structure.

americas-natchez-chiefdom.rationale: Bbox [-92.99, 30.01, -89.01, 33.99] covers Lower Mississippi Valley region including the Natchez Bluffs (modern Natchez, MS area near 31.6N/-91.4W) and associated villages. Slightly over-extends north and west but acceptable as the Natchez political/cultural area at contact. HBM 'Natchez' (1500) extends broader [-95.41, 29.06, -82.52, 35.30] covering all Natchezan-speaking groups.

americas-chibcha-muisca.rationale: Current bbox [-75.56, 3.68, -71.54, 7.23] is slightly over-extended (east into the llanos). Replace with HBM 'Muisca' (1492) polygon (bbox [-74.68, 4.15, -72.47, 6.99]) which tightly fits the Eastern Cordillera highlands of Cundinamarca and Boyacá — the Muisca/Chibcha confederations of Bogotá (Bacatá) and Tunja (Hunza).
sources: Langebaek, C. (1992). Noticias de caciques muy mayores.

americas-mississippian-cahokia.rationale: Bbox [-92.0, 36.0, -87.5, 40.0] covers the Cahokia core in the American Bottom (Illinois opposite St. Louis) and the immediate Mississippian sphere of the central Mississippi Valley. Note: Cahokia was a city-state and its regional polities, NOT an empire — name and dashed border are appropriate.
sources: Pauketat, T. (2009). Cahokia: Ancient America's Great City on the Mississippi.

americas-ancestral-puebloan-chaco.rationale: Bbox [-109.49, 34.70, -106.51, 37.30] covers Chaco Canyon (NW New Mexico) and its great-house outlier network across the San Juan Basin into adjacent SW Colorado, SE Utah, NE Arizona. Canonical Chaco Phenomenon extent.
sources: Lekson, S. (2006). The Archaeology of Chaco Canyon.

americas-chimu-north-coast.rationale: Bbox [-80.56, -10.41, -76.04, -4.90] covers Peru's north coast from Tumbes (~-3.5N) south to ~-10.4N (around Casma/Chillón). At peak (~1470), Chimú extended from Tumbes to the Chillón valley near Lima (~-11.7N) — current geometry slightly truncates the southern frontier but is acceptable.
sources: Moseley, M. & Day, K. (1982). Chan Chan: Andean Desert City.

americas-toltec-empire.rationale: Current bbox [-101.99, 17.51, -96.16, 22.49] is plausible but extends slightly too far south. Replace with HBM 'Toltec Empire' (1000) polygon (bbox [-100.65, 18.35, -97.55, 21.62]) which tightly captures the Tula core in Hidalgo plus extensions into Estado de México, Tlaxcala, and Puebla. Note: Toltec political reach beyond Hidalgo is debated.
sources: Diehl, R. (1983). Tula: The Toltec Capital of Ancient Mexico.

chimu-empire.rationale: Duplicate of americas-chimu-north-coast. Current bbox [-80.07, -12.76, -76.40, -6.76] over-extends south to -12.76 (south Lima coast) — Chimú peak southern frontier was the Chillón valley (~-11.7N). Replace with HBM 'Chimú Empire' (1300) polygon bbox [-80.07, -12.76, -76.40, -6.76] which is also slightly over-extended but is the canonical reference. Recommend deduplicating with americas-chimu-north-coast.

americas-itza-kingdom.rationale: Bbox [-90.0, 15.04, -88.23, 18.99] covers the Petén lakes region of northern Guatemala — Itza homeland centered on Lake Petén Itzá (Nojpetén/Tayasal, last independent Maya kingdom, conquered 1697).
sources: Jones, G. (1998). The Conquest of the Last Maya Kingdom.

americas-kowoj-kingdom.rationale: Current bbox [-90.0, 14.39, -88.22, 17.99] extends south to 14.4N into the Guatemalan highlands — Kowoj was a Petén lowland polity around Lakes Macanché and Yaxhá. Recommend tightening southern bound to ~16.5N. (Geometry itself may already be clipped to country borders; verify and tighten.)
sources: Rice, P. & Rice, D. (2009). The Kowoj: Identity, Migration, and Geopolitics in Late Postclassic Petén.

americas-mixtec-kingdoms.rationale: Bbox [-98.79, 16.01, -95.21, 18.99] covers the Mixteca regions (Mixteca Alta, Mixteca Baja, Mixteca de la Costa) of western Oaxaca, southern Puebla, and eastern Guerrero. Aligns with HBM 'Mixtec Empire' (1300-1500) bbox [-102.62, 17.49, -98.70, 21.02] (HBM is broader as it includes Mixtec sphere of influence).
sources: Spores, R. (1984). The Mixtecs in Ancient and Colonial Times.

americas-mixtec-confederation.rationale: Near-duplicate of americas-mixtec-kingdoms. Same audit conclusion. Recommend deduplicating in source data.

americas-taino-chiefdoms.rationale: Bbox [-84.95, 17.60, -65.27, 26.93] covers the Greater Antilles (Cuba, Hispaniola, Jamaica, Puerto Rico) and Bahamas — the canonical pre-contact Taíno (Arawak) range. HBM 'Taino' (1492) polygon is somewhat broader, extending into Lesser Antilles fringe.
sources: Rouse, I. (1992). The Tainos: Rise and Decline of the People Who Greeted Columbus.

americas-mississippian-peak.rationale: Bbox [-95.2, 30.4, -79.5, 39.8] correctly covers the Mississippian Interaction Sphere at peak — from the middle Mississippi Valley east to the Atlantic Piedmont (Etowah, Moundville, etc.), south to the Gulf Coast. Note: 'Confederacy' in the name is misleading — Mississippian was a network of chiefdoms, not a unified polity. Recommend renaming to 'Mississippian Interaction Sphere' or 'Mississippian Cultures'.
sources: Pauketat, T. (2004). Ancient Cahokia and the Mississippians.

americas-inca-kingdom-cusco.rationale: Bbox [-72.5, -14.3, -70.5, -12.3] covers the pre-imperial Kingdom of Cusco (~1200-1438) in the Urubamba/Vilcanota valley — the Inca dynastic homeland prior to Pachacuti's expansion. Geometry appropriate as a small pre-state polity.
sources: Bauer, B. (2004). Ancient Cuzco: Heartland of the Inca.

americas-mayapan-confederacy.rationale: Current bbox [-87.99, 19.27, -86.83, 20.99] is too narrow — covers only eastern Yucatán. Mayapan was the political center of the so-called 'League of Mayapan' covering most of northern Yucatán peninsula (Yucatán state + parts of Quintana Roo and Campeche). Recommend expanding west to ~-90W, south to ~19N. Geometry needs widening — flagged as upgrade-needed.
sources: Pollock, H. et al. (1962). Mayapan, Yucatan, Mexico.
Masson, M. & Peraza Lope, C. (2014). Kukulcan's Realm: Urban Life at Ancient Mayapán.

americas-huron-wendat.rationale: Current bbox [-82.49, 43.51, -77.51, 46.49] is much larger than the actual Huron homeland (Wendake) which was a compact territory of ~880 km^2 between Lake Simcoe and Georgian Bay (approximately 44.3-44.9N, -80.0 to -79.4W). Bbox may represent broader Wendat/Tionontate/Petun influence sphere. Recommend tightening to Wendake homeland (~44N-45N, -80.5W to -79W) and using dashed style to indicate uncertain extended influence.
sources: Trigger, B. (1976). The Children of Aataentsic: A History of the Huron People.

americas-tarascan-purepecha.rationale: Bbox [-103.99, 17.51, -99.01, 21.49] covers the Tarascan (Purépecha) state centered on Lake Pátzcuaro — Michoacán proper with extensions west to Pacific (Costa Grande de Guerrero), north into Guanajuato, east to the Aztec frontier. The Tarascans successfully resisted Aztec conquest, holding a fortified frontier zone.
sources: Pollard, H. (1993). Tariácuri's Legacy: The Prehispanic Tarascan State.

americas-tlaxcala.rationale: Bbox [-98.60, 18.90, -97.40, 19.90] closely matches the territory of the four Tlaxcalteca cabeceras (Tepeticpac, Ocotelulco, Quiahuiztlán, Tizatlán) corresponding to modern Tlaxcala state. CRITICAL: Tlaxcala was an independent indigenous enclave surrounded by Aztec tributary provinces but NEVER conquered by the Triple Alliance — a load-bearing fact for any Aztec-empire map and for the Spanish-Tlaxcalan alliance of 1519.
sources: Gibson, C. (1952). Tlaxcala in the Sixteenth Century.

americas-coosa-chiefdom.rationale: Bbox [-87.49, 32.01, -83.48, 35.99] covers the Coosa paramount chiefdom in the Coosa-Tennessee river valleys spanning NW Georgia, NE Alabama, and E Tennessee. Documented by Hernando de Soto entrada (1540) chronicles as the most powerful chiefdom in the interior Southeast.
sources: Hudson, C. et al. (1985). Coosa: A Chiefdom in the 16th-century Southeastern United States. American Antiquity 50.
Smith, M. (2000). Coosa: The Rise and Fall of a Southeastern Mississippian Chiefdom.

americas-tupinamba-confederation.rationale: Current bbox [-51.99, -25.98, -46.01, -18.02] covers the southern Tupinambá coast (modern Espírito Santo, Rio de Janeiro, São Paulo state). However, Tupinambá-speaking peoples occupied a longer Atlantic coastal strip from Pernambuco/Paraíba (~-7N) south to Paraná (~-25.5S). Recommend extending bbox north along the Brazilian coast to capture northern Tupinambá groups (Tabajara, Potiguara, Caeté).
sources: Fausto, C. (2000). Of Enemies and Pets: Warfare and Shamanism in Amazonia.
Métraux, A. (1928). La civilisation matérielle des tribus tupi-guarani.

americas-aztec-expansion.rationale: Bbox [-103.48, 15.66, -92.52, 21.98] is a reasonable Aztec maximum extent for ~1519. Covers central Mexico from Pacific Guerrero coast to Gulf Veracruz, south to Soconusco province (Pacific Chiapas, ~14N), north to Hidalgo/Tampico Huasteca. CRITICAL caveats for the polygon: must EXCLUDE (1) Tlaxcala enclave (independent), (2) Tarascan/Purépecha kingdom (all of Michoacán, never conquered), (3) Yopitzinco (highland Guerrero, independent), (4) Metztitlan and Tutotepec/Tlapanec strongholds. Verify these holes in the actual polygon.
sources: Berdan, F. & Anawalt, P. (1992). The Codex Mendoza.
Hassig, R. (1988). Aztec Warfare: Imperial Expansion and Political Control.

aztec-empire.rationale: Duplicate of americas-aztec-expansion with crude geometry. Current bbox [-105.51, 16.17, -93.74, 22.90] extends too far west (-105.5 is in Nayarit/Sinaloa coast, well into Tarascan and independent western Mexican territory). Replace with HBM 'Aztec Empire' (1500) polygon — which itself has the same bbox but more faithful coastline coordinates. Verify (and add holes for) Tlaxcala, Tarascan/Purépecha, Yopitzinco enclaves.

americas-inca-tawantinsuyu.rationale: Bbox [-91.67, -38.27, -57.47, 3.34] roughly correct for Inca Empire peak (~1525): north to Pasto/southern Colombia (3.34N ✓), south to the Maule River in central Chile (~-35.3; current -38.27 over-extends into Mapuche territory which Inca failed to conquer), east to the eastern Andean slope in Bolivia/NW Argentina (~-64W; current -57.47 over-extends into the Paraguayan Chaco/Argentine Pampa which Inca did NOT reach). CRITICAL: Inca did NOT control the Amazon basin or extend east of the Andes beyond NW Argentina/Bolivia/Tucumán. Recommend tightening eastern frontier to ~-64W and southern frontier to ~-35.5S.
sources: Rowe, J. (1946). Inca Culture at the Time of the Spanish Conquest. Handbook of South American Indians vol 2.
Bauer, B. & Smit, D. (2015). Vilcabamba and the Archaeology of Inca Resistance.

inca-empire.rationale: Duplicate of americas-inca-tawantinsuyu with simpler geometry. Bbox [-81.42, -37.28, -65.49, 0.82] has cleaner eastern frontier (-65.49 ≈ eastern Andes) but southern extent (-37.28) still over-extends past the Maule River. Recommend tightening south to ~-35.5 and deduplicating.

americas-iroquois-confederacy.rationale: Bbox [-80.48, 39.72, -71.86, 44.49] covers the Iroquois (Haudenosaunee) Five/Six Nations homeland in upstate New York with the post-Beaver-Wars (1640-1700) sphere of influence extending into Pennsylvania, southern Ontario, and parts of Ohio/Michigan. After ~1700 the Confederacy held tributary or hegemonic claims over a much wider region. HBM 'Iroquois' (1500) bbox [-77.28, 41.18, -66.83, 46.20] is more limited to the homeland. Either acceptable; current geometry reflects peak influence circa late-17th century.
sources: Engelbrecht, W. (2003). Iroquoia: The Development of a Native World.
Fenton, W. (1998). The Great Law and the Longhouse.

americas-apache-confederacy.rationale: Current bbox [-111.58, 30.01, -106.32, 31.78] is grossly under-extended — covers only a thin AZ-NM-Sonora-Chihuahua border strip. Apache range encompassed multiple Apachean groups: Western Apache (AZ), Chiricahua (SE AZ, SW NM, N Sonora), Mescalero (E NM, W TX, N Chihuahua), Jicarilla (N NM, S CO), Lipan (Texas/N Coahuila), and Plains Apache/Kiowa-Apache (SW Plains). Replace with HBM 'Apache' (1500) polygon (bbox [-112.72, 26.09, -101.07, 33.15]) which captures most Apachean groups; note that northern Jicarilla/Plains Apache may extend to ~37N in southern Colorado. Border kept dashed because Apachean groups were highly mobile and territorial boundaries were fluid.
sources: Opler, M. (1983). 'Apachean Cultural Pattern and Its Origins'. Handbook of North American Indians vol. 10: Southwest.

americas-mapuche-araucania.rationale: Bbox [-73.84, -41.98, -70.36, -34.02] covers central-south Chile from approximately the Maule region (~-34S) south to Chiloé (~-42S). Captures the canonical Wallmapu (Mapuche homeland) west of the Andes. MISSING: post-1600s 'Mapuchización' of the Patagonian pampas east of the Andes (puelche-mapuche/pehuenche) into modern Neuquén and Río Negro provinces of Argentina. HBM 'Wallmapu (Mapuche)' (1492) bbox [-74.30, -44.41, -56.70, -30.46] includes the eastern extension. For an empire spanning 1500-1883, recommend extending east to ~-67W to capture trans-Andean Mapuche.
sources: Bengoa, J. (2003). Historia de los antiguos mapuches del sur.
Boccara, G. (1998). Guerre et ethnogenèse mapuche dans le Chili colonial.

americas-patagonia-tehuelche.rationale: Bbox [-75.71, -52.98, -63.58, -38.03] covers Patagonia south of the Río Colorado/Río Negro through to Tierra del Fuego — the range of the Aónikenk (Southern Tehuelche/Chónik) and Mecharnúe (Northern Tehuelche/Gününa Küne). HBM 'Aónikenk (Tehuelche)' (1492) bbox [-74.45, -52.85, -64.40, -41.52] is similar.
sources: Casamiquela, R. (1985). Bosquejo de una etnología de la Provincia del Neuquén.

americas-powhatan-confederacy.rationale: Bbox [-78.79, 36.54, -75.29, 38.99] covers Tsenacommacah, the Powhatan paramountcy's territory in Tidewater Virginia (Chesapeake Bay drainage east of the Fall Line). Slight over-extension south into NC Albemarle region but acceptable.
sources: Rountree, H. (1989). The Powhatan Indians of Virginia.

americas-comancheria.rationale: Current geometry from HBM 'Comanche' (1500) is grossly under-extended (bbox [-103.00, 28.30, -94.84, 33.73]) — that represents early Comanche range, not the peak Comancheria of 1750-1850. Peak Comancheria extended from southern Kansas (~38N) and SE Colorado in the north, west into eastern New Mexico, east to the Cross Timbers of Oklahoma/Texas, south to the Edwards Plateau and Rio Grande borderlands. Replace with hand-traced polygon matching Pekka Hämäläinen's 'Comanche Empire' map.
sources: Hämäläinen, P. (2008). The Comanche Empire. Yale.
Kavanagh, T. (1996). The Comanches: A History 1706-1875.

americas-lakota-sioux.rationale: Bbox [-108.0, 41.5, -96.5, 49.0] covers the Lakota homeland on the northern Great Plains: Dakotas, eastern Montana, eastern Wyoming, northern Nebraska. Matches the seven Lakota council fires' (Oceti Sakowin) range at 1750-1877 peak. Dashed border appropriate for mobile/hunting territory.
sources: Hämäläinen, P. (2019). Lakota America: A New History of Indigenous Power.
DeMallie, R. (2001). Handbook of North American Indians vol. 13: Plains.

americas-mexican-empire-iturbide.rationale: First Mexican Empire (1821-1823) under Agustín de Iturbide. Bbox [-118.86, 8.03, -82.57, 40.53] is reasonable: covered all of modern Mexico plus Central America (Captaincy General of Guatemala — modern Guatemala, El Salvador, Honduras, Nicaragua, Costa Rica) which joined the empire briefly in 1821-1823. Northern extent (40.53N) covers the Alta California/Texas/New Mexico inheritance from New Spain.
sources: Anna, T. (1990). The Mexican Empire of Iturbide.

americas-mexican-republic-1824.rationale: First Mexican Republic (1824-1848). Bbox [-118.86, 8.03, -82.57, 40.53] covers the territory inherited from the First Mexican Empire after Central America seceded (1823-1824). NOTE: Same bbox/geometry as americas-mexican-empire-iturbide which is incorrect — the Republic LOST Central America in 1823-1824 (forming the Federal Republic of Central America). The 8.03N southern extent should be removed for the Republic. Recommend re-clipping the southern boundary at the modern Guatemala-Mexico border (~14.5N) plus Chiapas which was retained.

british-empire-1815.rationale:
British Empire (1815) polygon includes the post-Napoleonic gains (Cape Colony from 1806, Ceylon, Mauritius, Malta, Heligoland) and the core empire (British Isles, Canada including Rupert's Land, Indian Company holdings in Bengal/Madras/Bombay, Australia colonies). The polygon correctly excludes the now-independent United States, Mexico, Hong Kong (not until 1842), Singapore (only 1819), and most of Africa.


Key findings:
  - [NOTABLE] india_partial; observed=Delhi INSIDE; expected=Delhi NOT under EIC in 1815 (taken from Marathas 1803, but Delhi as Mughal capital under EIC protection); Delhi being inside is technically defensible: the EIC took Delhi in 1803 (Second Anglo-Maratha War) and held it under "protection" of the Mughal emperor. The dataset chooses to include it — accept as accurate for the 1815 audit_year.


Proposed remediation: No substantive change. Ensure coastal vertices on Nova Scotia and Cape Province include Halifax and Cape Town.

americas-argentine-confederation.rationale:
Argentine Confederation (1816-1861) polygon covers the United Provinces of the Rio de la Plata at their consolidation phase — Buenos Aires, Cordoba, Mendoza, Salta, Posadas all inside. Uruguay (Montevideo) and Paraguay (Asuncion) correctly excluded (independent 1828 and 1811 respectively). Chile, Bolivia, Brazil also correctly excluded.


Proposed remediation: Verify the southern boundary: for 1816-1861 the effective southern frontier was around the Rio Negro. Polygons including all of present-day Patagonia would over-extend.

americas-gran-colombia.rationale:
Gran Colombia (1819-1831) polygon correctly spans modern Venezuela, Colombia, Ecuador, and Panama (Bogota, Caracas, Quito, Panama City inside). Peru, Bolivia, Chile, Argentina, Mexico, Central America correctly outside. Disputed northwest (Guajira / parts of Esequibo) not tested.


Proposed remediation: No change. Optional: verify the Essequibo region (modern Guyana west bank) is treated per the Gran-Colombian / Venezuelan claim.

americas-united-states-1848.rationale:
United States (1848) polygon depicts the country immediately after the Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo (Feb 2, 1848): the 13 colonies + Northwest Ordinance + Louisiana Purchase + Texas annexation (1845) + Oregon (1846) + Mexican Cession (Feb 1848 — California, Nevada, Utah, most of Arizona, New Mexico, parts of Colorado/Wyoming/Kansas/Oklahoma). All major US cities inside (Boston, Philadelphia, New York, Washington DC, Atlanta, Charleston, Mobile, Nashville, New Orleans, St Louis, Houston, San Antonio, Austin, Dallas, San Francisco, Los Angeles, San Diego, Portland OR, Salt Lake City, Denver, Chicago, Detroit, Cincinnati, Pittsburgh). Tucson/Tombstone correctly excluded (Gadsden Purchase 1854).


Proposed remediation: No change.

americas-empire-of-brazil.rationale:
Empire of Brazil (1822-1889) polygon covers most of modern Brazil — Rio de Janeiro, Sao Paulo, Salvador, Recife, Manaus inside. Issues: Belem (Para state capital) tests outside — coastal precision; Acre (in NW Brazil) is INSIDE but Acre was Bolivian until the 1903 Treaty of Petropolis, so for the 1822-1889 Empire span it should be OUTSIDE.


Key findings:
  - [NOTABLE] acre_inside; observed=Acre BR INSIDE; expected=Acre OUTSIDE (Bolivian until 1903; Brazilian thereafter); The 1822-1889 Empire of Brazil polygon should exclude Acre and follow the pre-1903 Bolivian/Peruvian boundary in the southwest Amazon.


Proposed remediation: Trim the western boundary in Acre to follow the pre-1903 line (roughly the Madeira-Mamore meridian and the Javari headwaters). Fix Belem coastal vertices.

british-empire-1837.rationale:
British Empire (1837) — Victorian accession date — captures British Isles, all of Canada, expanded Indian holdings (Delhi, Bombay, Madras, Calcutta), Cape Colony, Mauritius, Ceylon, Australia, NZ from 1840. The 1837 polygon does not yet include Hong Kong (1842), Singapore (correctly 1819 — depends on inclusion), Lower Burma (1852), or any African interior. Coastal-point misses on Halifax and Cape Town again.


Proposed remediation: No substantive change.

french-colonial.rationale:
French Colonial Empire (Africa) — scope per the dataset is Africa only ("French Colonial Empire (Africa)"). The polygon includes Algeria, Tunisia, Morocco protectorate, French West Africa (Dakar, Bamako, Niamey, Conakry, Abidjan), French Equatorial Africa (Yaounde absent — see below — Libreville, Brazzaville), and Madagascar. Indochina (Hanoi/Saigon/Phnom Penh/Vientiane) and the Levant mandate (Damascus/Beirut) are correctly outside the AFRICA-scoped polygon. Note: Yaounde (Cameroon) tests outside; French Cameroun mandate from 1919 should include Yaounde.


Key findings:
  - [NOTABLE] yaounde_inside; observed=Yaounde OUTSIDE; expected=Yaounde INSIDE for the audit_year 1930 (French Cameroun mandate 1919-1960); Most of Cameroon was French Mandate from 1919 onward.


Proposed remediation: Add Cameroun mandate polygon to the MultiPolygon; verify French Guinea coastal vertex set includes Conakry; consider renaming the dataset entry to clarify Africa-only scope or split into separate non-African layers for Indochina/Levant.

americas-republic-of-texas.rationale:
Republic of Texas (1836-1845) polygon covers the area between the Sabine and the Rio Grande, north to the Red River. Houston, San Antonio, Austin, Dallas all inside. The Texan claim extended west to the upper Rio Grande into modern-day New Mexico (including Santa Fe), but this area was never effectively controlled and was relinquished in the 1850 Compromise.


Proposed remediation: No change required. Optional: clearly label whether the polygon depicts the *claimed* (full strip to upper Rio Grande, including Santa Fe area) or *controlled* (east of the upper Pecos) extent.

americas-republic-of-yucatan.rationale:
Republic of Yucatan (1841-1848) polygon covers the Yucatan peninsula (Merida and Campeche inside). Mexico City, Guadalajara, Veracruz, Belize, Guatemala correctly outside.


Proposed remediation: No change.

americas-mexico-1848.rationale:
Mexico (1848) polygon depicts Mexico's reduced boundary after the Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo (Feb 1848), losing all territory north of the Gila/Rio Grande line. Includes the central/southern states (Mexico City, Guadalajara, Monterrey) but Veracruz and Tucson/Tombstone (Gadsden region pre-1854) test outside — Veracruz is a coastal precision miss; the Gadsden area should be INSIDE for 1848-1853 (it was Mexican until the 1854 Gadsden Purchase).


Key findings:
  - [NOTABLE] gadsden_pre_1854; observed=Tucson, Tombstone OUTSIDE; expected=INSIDE for 1848-1853 portion of the date range (1848-1900). After 1854 they correctly belong to the US.; If the polygon is for the entire 1848-1900 span, it should match the 1854+ boundary (Gadsden excluded). If it is the snapshot in 1848, Gadsden should be included.


Proposed remediation: Decide on snapshot year (1848 vs 1854+) and adjust the northwest border accordingly. Fix Veracruz vertex precision.

americas-united-states-1860.rationale:
United States (1860) polygon depicts the contiguous US just before the Civil War — includes Gadsden Purchase (1854; Tucson inside). Excludes Alaska (Russian until 1867), Hawaii (annexed 1898), and the Mexican territories south of the Gadsden line. All expected cities behave correctly.


Proposed remediation: No change.

africa-ethiopian-empire-menelik.rationale:
Ethiopian Empire (Menelik II expansion, 1855-1936) polygon covers the highlands and the Menelik-era southward conquests (Harar, Oromia, Sidamo). Addis Ababa correctly inside. Asmara (Eritrea) tests INSIDE the polygon — that's wrong: Eritrea was an Italian colony from 1890 onward (formal proclamation 1 January 1890), so for most of the 1855-1936 span Asmara should be OUTSIDE.


Key findings:
  - [NOTABLE] asmara_inside; observed=Asmara INSIDE; expected=Asmara OUTSIDE (Italian Eritrea 1890-1941; for the post-1890 portion of the date range, it should be outside); Pre-1890 (during Menelik's coronation 1889) Eritrea was contested. Post-Treaty of Wuchale (1889) and the 1896 Battle of Adwa, Eritrea remained Italian.


Proposed remediation: Trim the polygon along the Mareb river to exclude Italian Eritrea (Asmara). The 1896 Treaty of Addis Ababa fixed the Eritrean boundary at the Mareb-Belesa-Muna line.

british-empire-1858.rationale:
British Empire (1858) marks the start of direct Crown rule over India after the East India Company's abolition. Polygon includes British Isles, Canada, all of India (Delhi, Mumbai, Madras, Calcutta), Cape Colony, Australia, NZ. Issues: Singapore, Hong Kong, and Halifax all test outside the polygon — Singapore (1819) and Hong Kong (1842) should be inside, suggesting either small-island precision issues OR the polygon omits these strategic outposts.


Key findings:
  - [NOTABLE] singapore_inside; observed=Singapore OUTSIDE; expected=Singapore INSIDE (Straits Settlements; British since 1819)
  - [NOTABLE] hong_kong_inside; observed=Hong Kong OUTSIDE; expected=Hong Kong INSIDE (ceded 1842)


Proposed remediation: Ensure the polygon includes Singapore island and Hong Kong island as discrete MultiPolygon members. Check for missing dependencies: Penang, Malacca, Labuan.

americas-confederate-states.rationale:
Confederate States polygon covers the 11 states (VA, NC, SC, GA, FL, AL, MS, LA, TX, AR, TN). Bbox extends west to ~-103°E which suggests inclusion of the Confederate claim to Arizona Territory (south of the 34th parallel) and Indian Territory. Atlanta, Charleston, Mobile, Nashville, New Orleans, Little Rock, Houston, San Antonio, Austin, Dallas, Memphis all inside. Issue: Richmond (the Confederate capital!) tests OUTSIDE the polygon, likely a vertex-precision issue at the Virginia/Chesapeake coastline. Federal cities (Washington DC, Boston, NY, Chicago, Philadelphia, Pittsburgh) correctly outside. Santa Fe correctly outside (despite Confederate claim, never controlled).


Key findings:
  - [NOTABLE] richmond_inside; observed=Richmond OUTSIDE; expected=Richmond INSIDE (Confederate capital, in Virginia); Likely a small precision miss along the Chesapeake/James River coastline. Definite fix.


Proposed remediation: Adjust the Virginia coastal polygon to ensure Richmond at (-77.46, 37.54) is enclosed.

austro-hungarian.rationale:
Austro-Hungarian polygon captures Austria + Hungary + Bohemia/Moravia + Slovakia + Galicia + Transylvania + Slovenia + Croatia + Trentino + Trieste. Bosnia (Sarajevo) is NOT inside — this is technically incomplete for 1908-1918 when Bosnia-Herzegovina was formally annexed (and de-facto administered from 1878). The polygon also shows the city of Belgrade marginally inside (a simplification artifact: Zemun across the Sava/Danube was Hungarian, and the simplified polygon sweeps in the Belgrade point). HBM 1900 reference shows the same artifact.


Key findings:
  - [NOTABLE] bosnia_inside; observed=Sarajevo OUTSIDE; expected=Sarajevo INSIDE (annexed 1908; condominium from 1878); For audit_year 1908-1918 Bosnia-Herzegovina should be included.


Proposed remediation: Optional: union with Bosnia-Herzegovina polygon (HBM has Bosnia under Ottoman until 1878; in 1900 it should be Austria-Hungary admin). Trim the Belgrade-area sliver if a higher-fidelity Sava/Danube border is needed.

german-empire.rationale:
German Empire polygon centred on Germany proper (Prussia, Bavaria, etc.) is largely correct (Berlin, Hamburg, Munich, Frankfurt, Cologne, Strasbourg, Konigsberg, Danzig, Poznan all inside). Two issues: (1) Metz tests outside our polygon — Metz/Alsace-Lorraine was annexed in 1871 and should be inside (the polygon may exclude the immediate Metz area due to simplification); (2) Warsaw tests INSIDE our polygon, but Warsaw was inside the Russian Empire (Congress Poland) throughout 1871-1918 — this is a clear overcount in the eastern frontier.


Key findings:
  - [CRITICAL] warsaw_inside; observed=Warsaw INSIDE; expected=Warsaw OUTSIDE (Russian-ruled Congress Poland 1815-1918); Indicates the east boundary has crept too far east. The German Empire eastern boundary ran roughly along the Prosna and along East Prussia, not encompassing Warsaw.
  - [NOTABLE] metz_inside; observed=Metz OUTSIDE; expected=Metz INSIDE (Alsace-Lorraine annexed 1871-1918); Strasbourg is inside, so most of Alsace-Lorraine is captured; Metz exclusion likely a vertex-sparse simplification artifact along the western edge.


Proposed remediation: Re-derive the 1871-1918 German Empire polygon by intersecting modern Germany + Alsace-Lorraine + former eastern territories (Posen, West Prussia, Silesia, East Prussia) but EXCLUDING Congress Poland east of the Prosna. Refer to HBM world_1900.geojson:Germany or use the canonical 1871-1918 borders from Wikipedia (German Empire administrative map).

british-empire-1880.rationale:
British Empire (1880) at the start of high imperialism. Polygon captures Canada, India, Australia, NZ, Cape Colony. Missing on point-tests: Singapore, Hong Kong, Cape Town (coastal), Lagos (annexed 1861), Accra (Gold Coast from 1874). These suggest the polygon omits several West-African and Asian coastal/island holdings.


Key findings:
  - [NOTABLE] singapore_hong_kong; observed=Both OUTSIDE; expected=Both INSIDE
  - [NOTABLE] lagos_accra; observed=Both OUTSIDE; expected=Lagos (annexed 1861) and Accra (Gold Coast Colony 1874) INSIDE


Proposed remediation: Augment with Singapore + Penang + Malacca + Labuan + Hong Kong + Lagos Colony + Gold Coast + Sierra Leone + Gambia. Add British Honduras (Belize, since 1862), British Guiana, and Caribbean island colonies if not present.

british-colonial-africa.rationale:
British Colonial Africa polygon spans the British African empire from 1880 to decolonization in 1968. It includes Egypt+Sudan, Kenya, Uganda, S. Africa, Rhodesias, Nyasaland, Nigeria (Cairo, Khartoum, Pretoria, Nairobi, Kampala, Salisbury, Lusaka, Lilongwe). Coastal misses: Cape Town, Lagos, Mombasa. Correctly excludes Algiers, Tripoli, Dakar, Yaounde, Kinshasa, Dar es Salaam (German then mandate), Luanda, Maputo, Antananarivo.


Key findings:
  - [NOTABLE] cape_town_lagos_mombasa; observed=OUTSIDE; expected=INSIDE — coastal point precision


Proposed remediation: Fix coastal vertex precision for Cape Town, Lagos, Mombasa. Decide whether to include British mandate Tanganyika; if so add it for the post-1919 portion of the date range.

italian-colonial-africa.rationale:
Italian Colonial Africa polygon includes Libya (Tripoli, Benghazi) and likely Eritrea coast, but Asmara, Mogadishu, and Addis Ababa all test outside. For the 1882-1947 span, the empire should at minimum include: Eritrea (1882-1941), Italian Somaliland (1889-1941), Libya (1911-1943), and Italian East Africa = Ethiopia + Eritrea + Somaliland (1936-1941).


Key findings:
  - [NOTABLE] eritrea; observed=Asmara OUTSIDE; expected=Asmara INSIDE (Italian Eritrea 1882-1941)
  - [NOTABLE] somaliland; observed=Mogadishu OUTSIDE; expected=Mogadishu INSIDE (Italian Somaliland 1889-1941)
  - [NOTABLE] aoi_ethiopia; observed=Addis Ababa OUTSIDE; expected=Addis Ababa INSIDE for 1936-1941 (Italian East Africa); excluded otherwise; For an empire spanning 1882-1947 with peak in 1938, AOI should be inside.


Proposed remediation: Add MultiPolygon parts for Eritrea, Italian Somaliland, and Italian Ethiopia (1936-41). Source: HBM world_1938.geojson features under SUBJECTO=ITALY.

german-colonial-empire.rationale:
German Colonial Empire polygon captures the major African possessions (Kamerun, Togo, German South-West Africa, German East Africa). Pacific possessions (German Samoa/Apia, German New Guinea, Caroline Islands, Marshall Islands, Mariana Islands incl. Saipan, Truk/Chuuk, Yap, Palau) all test outside — the polygon does not include Germany's Pacific island colonies, which were a significant part of the empire 1884-1914.


Key findings:
  - [NOTABLE] apia_inside; observed=Apia OUTSIDE; expected=Apia INSIDE (German Samoa 1900-1914)
  - [NOTABLE] truk_inside; observed=Truk OUTSIDE; expected=Truk INSIDE (Caroline Islands, German 1899-1914)
  - [NOTABLE] yap_inside; observed=Yap OUTSIDE; expected=Yap INSIDE


Proposed remediation: Augment with MultiPolygon parts for German Samoa, German New Guinea (Kaiser-Wilhelmsland), Bismarck Archipelago, Solomon Islands (Bougainville/Buka, Choiseul, Santa Isabel until 1899), Caroline Islands, Marshall Islands, Mariana Islands (excl. Guam), Kiautschou Bay (Tsingtao) concession. Source: HBM 1914 features carrying SUBJECTO=GERMAN EMPIRE on Pacific islands; or Wikipedia "German colonial empire".

belgian-congo.rationale:
Belgian Congo polygon (1885 Congo Free State -> 1908 Belgian Congo -> 1960 independence as DRC) correctly traces the modern DRC outline. Belgium (Brussels) correctly excluded. Brazzaville (French Congo, across the Congo River from Kinshasa) tests INSIDE — that's a precision artifact: the Brazzaville-Kinshasa river boundary is very narrow and the simplified polygon overshoots. Ruanda-Urundi (post-WWI Belgian mandate) is excluded — defensible since it was a separate mandate, but historically tied to the Belgian colonial system.


Proposed remediation: Refine the Congo River boundary near Pool Malebo so that Brazzaville falls on the French (north) side. Optionally add Ruanda-Urundi as a separate sister layer.

empire-of-japan-1895.rationale:
Empire of Japan (1895) polygon correctly includes the Japanese home islands plus Taiwan (acquired from China via Treaty of Shimonoseki, April 1895). Excludes Korea, Manchuria, China proper, Philippines — all correct for this period (Korea protectorate only 1905, annexed 1910).


Proposed remediation: No change. Optional: include the Pescadores (Penghu) Islands explicitly if not already in the Taiwan polygon.

british-empire-1900.rationale:
British Empire (1900) — pre-WWI peak before mandates. Polygon includes Canada, India, Australia, NZ, South Africa (Cape + Natal + post-1902 Transvaal/OFS), Egypt, Sudan (Anglo-Egyptian condominium from 1899), Nigeria, Gold Coast, Kenya (East Africa Protectorate 1895), Rhodesia, Nyasaland. Missing: Singapore, Kuala Lumpur (Federated Malay States 1895), Hong Kong, Lagos, Mombasa.


Key findings:
  - [NOTABLE] malaya_singapore_hk; observed=Singapore, KL, Hong Kong OUTSIDE; expected=All INSIDE
  - [NOTABLE] lagos_mombasa; observed=OUTSIDE; expected=INSIDE (coastal city precision likely)


Proposed remediation: Same as 1880 (add Asian outposts). Confirm Nigeria coastal-bay polygon vertices include Lagos.

empire-of-japan-1910.rationale:
Empire of Japan (1910) polygon adds Korea (annexed August 1910 — Seoul and Pyongyang inside) to the 1895 extent. Manchuria, Beijing, Shanghai, Manila, Hanoi all correctly outside. Sakhalin southern half (post-1905 Treaty of Portsmouth) presumed inside the Japan home-islands polygon component.


Proposed remediation: Verify South Sakhalin (Karafuto) is included.

british-empire-1921.rationale:
British Empire (1921) — territorial peak after the WWI mandates (Iraq, Palestine, Transjordan, Tanganyika, parts of Cameroon and Togo) and incorporation of South West Africa via South African mandate. Polygon includes Baghdad, Jerusalem, Dar es Salaam, plus the pre-existing imperial core. Misses: Dublin (Irish Free State established Dec 1922 — for 1921 still British; the polygon may already reflect partition), Singapore, Hong Kong, Lagos (coastal).


Key findings:
  - [NOTABLE] singapore_hk; observed=OUTSIDE; expected=INSIDE


Proposed remediation: Add Singapore/HK islands, Lagos. Confirm Republic of Ireland is intentionally excluded.

empire-of-japan-1937.rationale:
Empire of Japan (1937) polygon adds Manchukuo (puppet state from 1932 — Mukden, Harbin, Port Arthur/Lushun all inside) to the 1910 extent. Beijing, Shanghai, Manila, Singapore, Hanoi correctly outside (Marco Polo Bridge July 1937; full North/East China occupation begins, but full Pacific war not until December 1941).


Proposed remediation: If the intent is to depict the "formal" Japanese empire (home + Korea + Taiwan + Manchukuo + Karafuto + South Pacific Mandate), the polygon is correct. If the intent is to include occupied China, extend to Beijing and the North China occupation. Choose one and document.

british-empire-1939.rationale:
British Empire (1939) — eve of WWII. Polygon includes Canada, India, Burma (separated from India 1937), Ceylon, Malaya (less Singapore on point test), Australia, NZ, South Africa, East/West/Southern Africa colonies, Palestine + Transjordan, Aden, Cyprus. Egypt and Iraq nominally independent — but Egypt is in the expected_out test (with caveat) and the polygon excludes Cairo. Misses: Dublin, Singapore, Hong Kong, Cairo, Lagos, Baghdad, Aden, plus a strange erroneous-inside on Dar es Salaam.


Key findings:
  - [NOTABLE] singapore_hk; observed=Singapore, HK OUTSIDE; expected=INSIDE
  - [NOTABLE] aden_lagos; observed=OUTSIDE; expected=INSIDE — coastal precision misses likely


Proposed remediation: Add Singapore + HK island polygons; ensure Aden and Lagos coastal points are inside the polygon vertices.

empire-of-japan-1942.rationale:
Empire of Japan (1942 peak) polygon includes home islands, Korea, Taiwan, Manchukuo, occupied China coast (Beijing, Shanghai), Hong Kong, Manila/Philippines, Malaya, Singapore (point test fails — see below), Indonesia/Jakarta, Burma/Rangoon, French Indochina/Hanoi/Saigon. Mainland coverage is correct. Coastal/island misses: Singapore, Hong Kong, Saipan, Guam — likely small-island precision issues.


Key findings:
  - [NOTABLE] singapore_hk; observed=Singapore, HK OUTSIDE on point test; expected=Both INSIDE (occupied Feb 1942 and Dec 1941 respectively)
  - [NOTABLE] mariana_caroline; observed=Saipan, Guam OUTSIDE; expected=Saipan INSIDE (Japanese-mandated since 1919); Guam INSIDE (occupied Dec 1941)


Proposed remediation: Add discrete island polygons for Singapore, Hong Kong island + Kowloon, Saipan/Tinian, Guam, Truk, Yap, Palau, Marshalls. The South Pacific Mandate islands (Class C League mandate after WWI) should already be inside as core Japan, not occupied.

third-reich-1938.rationale:
Third Reich (1938) polygon is identical to HBM world_1938.geojson "Germany". It correctly includes Berlin, Vienna (Anschluss March 1938), Munich, and the Sudetenland extension (Bratislava and other points east). It correctly excludes Prague, Warsaw, Paris, Brussels, etc. The HBM 1938 snapshot reflects the post-Munich (October 1938) boundary, which is the canonical interpretation for "1938". Note: Bratislava tests inside the polygon — by late 1938 Slovakia had autonomy but was not yet annexed; this slight overcount is inherited from the HBM source.


Proposed remediation: No structural change. Optionally clip out the small Slovakian protrusion containing Bratislava if strict end-1938 fidelity is desired.

third-reich-1939.rationale:
Third Reich (1939) polygon correctly extends to include Prague (Protectorate of Bohemia-Moravia, March 1939), Memel (March 1939), and Danzig (occupied September 1939). It correctly excludes Paris, Brussels, Amsterdam, Copenhagen, Oslo (those fell 1940). Bbox 5.9°E to 24.0°E reflects pre-Sept-1939 boundary; Poland east of the German-Soviet line is not yet inside, consistent with the snapshot before/at the start of WWII.


Proposed remediation: Verify Danzig (Gdansk) is included; if not, extend the polygon to include the Free City of Danzig area along the Polish corridor.

third-reich-1941.rationale:
Third Reich (1941) polygon depicts the peak of western/southern occupation prior to deep USSR penetration. Paris, Brussels, Amsterdam, Oslo, Belgrade, Athens all inside. Madrid, Stockholm, Helsinki, Moscow, London correctly outside. Bbox max latitude 71°N captures northern Norway. Copenhagen tests outside — this is suspicious because Denmark was occupied April 1940 and Copenhagen should be inside; likely a simplification gap at the Danish peninsula.


Key findings:
